संततं विपरीतं च कुर्वंति शब्दमुल्बणम् ॥
मूत्रश्लेष्मपुरीषाणां कुर्वंति भक्षणं मुदा ॥74॥
4.17.m:
Constantly they make unnatural and terrifying screams;
they eagerly consume urine, phlegm, and feces.

4.17.s:
mukhe tāsāṃ dadatyevamulkāṃ ca yamakiṃkarāḥ ..
bhuktvā bhogaṃ ca narake kṛmiyoniṃ prayāṃti tāḥ .. 75 ..
4.17.d:
मुखे तासां ददत्येवमुल्कां च यमकिंकराः ॥
भुक्त्वा भोगं च नरके कृमियोनिं प्रयांति ताः ॥ 75 ॥
4.17.m:
The servants of Yama place burning firebrands in their mouths;
having undergone suffering in hell, they enter the wombs of worms.

4.17.s:
bhakṣaṃti janmaśatakaṃ raktamāṃsapurīṣakam ..
śrutvāhaṃ viduṣāṃ vaktrādvedavākyeṣu niścitam .. 76 ..
4.17.d:
भक्षंति जन्मशतकं रक्तमांसपुरीषकम् ॥
श्रुत्वाहं विदुषां वक्त्राद्वेदवाक्येषु निश्चितम् ॥ 76 ॥
4.17.m:
For a hundred births they consume blood, flesh, and excrement.
Having heard the certainty in the words of the Vedas from the mouths of wise men,

4.17.s:
jānāmi kiṃcidabalā tvaṃ vedajanako vibhuḥ ..
gurorguruśca viduṣāṃ yogināṃ jñānināṃ tathā ..77..
4.17.d:
जानामि किंचिदबला त्वं वेदजनको विभुः ॥
गुरोर्गुरुश्च विदुषां योगिनां ज्ञानिनां तथा ॥77॥
4.17.m:
I, a weak woman, know a little; but you are the lord, the father of the Vedas,
the guru of gurus, and of the learned, the yogis, and the wise.

4.17.s:
sarvajñamevaṃbhūtaṃ tvāṃ bodhayāmi kimacyuta ..
prāṇādhiko'yaṃ kāṃto'yaṃ yadi mukto babhūva ha .. . 78 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वज्ञमेवंभूतं त्वां बोधयामि किमच्युत ॥
प्राणाधिकोऽयं कांतोऽयं यदि मुक्तो बभूव ह ॥ । 78 ॥
4.17.m:
How can I instruct you, O Acyuta, who are omniscient and so exalted?
If this beloved, who is dearer to me than life, should indeed become liberated,

4.17.s:
mama ko rakṣitā brahmandharmasya yauvanasya ca ..
kaumāre rakṣitā tāto dattvā pātrāya satkṛtī ..79..
4.17.d:
मम को रक्षिता ब्रह्मन्धर्मस्य यौवनस्य च ॥
कौमारे रक्षिता तातो दत्त्वा पात्राय सत्कृती ॥79॥
4.17.m:
who will be my protector, O Brahman, in respect to my virtue and my youth?
In childhood her father is her protector, having bestowed her upon a worthy man with honor;

4.17.s:
sarvadā rakṣitā kāṃtastadabhāve ca tatsutaḥ ..
triṣvavasthāsu nārīṇāṃ trātāraśca trayaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 4.17.80 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वदा रक्षिता कांतस्तदभावे च तत्सुतः ॥
त्रिष्ववस्थासु नारीणां त्रातारश्च त्रयः स्मृताः ॥ 4.17.80 ॥
4.17.m:
at all times her husband is her protector, and in his absence, her son.
In the three stages of life, women are declared to have three protectors.

4.17.s:
yāḥ svataṃtrāśca tā naṣṭāḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ ..
asatkulaprasūtāstāḥ kulaṭā duṣṭamānasāḥ .. 81 ..
4.17.d:
याः स्वतंत्राश्च ता नष्टाः सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृताः ॥
असत्कुलप्रसूतास्ताः कुलटा दुष्टमानसाः ॥ 81 ॥
4.17.m:
Those who are independent are ruined, cast out from all virtue;
born of a base family, they are unchaste and of evil mind.

4.17.s:
śatajanmakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ tāsāṃ naśyati padmaja ..
putrasneho yathā bālye tathā yūni ca vārddhake . .. 82 ..
4.17.d:
शतजन्मकृतं पुण्यं तासां नश्यति पद्मज ॥
पुत्रस्नेहो यथा बाल्ये तथा यूनि च वार्द्धके ॥। 82 ॥
4.17.m:
The merit accumulated by them in a hundred births is destroyed, O lotus-born one!
Just as there is affection for a son in childhood, so in youth and in old age;

4.17.s:
pativratānāṃ kānte ca sarvakāle samā spṛhā ..
sute stanaṃdhaye sneho mātṝṇāṃ cātiśobhite .. 83 ..
4.17.d:
पतिव्रतानां कान्ते च सर्वकाले समा स्पृहा ॥
सुते स्तनंधये स्नेहो मातॄणां चातिशोभिते ॥ 83 ॥
4.17.m:
for devoted wives, there is an equal longing for the husband at all times.
The affection of mothers for a suckling son is exceedingly beautiful,

4.17.s:
patisnehasya sādhvīnāṃ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm ..
stanāndhe stanadānāntamiṣṭānne bhojanāvadhi .. 84..
4.17.d:
पतिस्नेहस्य साध्वीनां कलां नार्हति षोडशीम् ॥

4.17.m:
yet it is not worth a sixteenth part of a virtuous woman's affection for her husband.

4.17.m:
the mind of chaste wives is constantly fixed on the husband, both in dream and in wakefulness.
Separation from relatives brings sorrow, and greater still is that from sons;

4.17.m:
separation from the husband is exceedingly terrible; there is no sorrow greater than this for a woman.
Just as an untaught woman might be burned in a blazing fire or by taking poison,

4.17.m:
so an intelligent woman is burned in the fire of separation from her beloved.
Virtuous women have no thirst for food or thirst for water without their husband;

4.17.s:

4.17.m:

There is no friend higher than the husband, nor anyone dearer than the husband;

there is no deity higher than the husband, nor any guru higher than the husband;

4.17.s:
na hi kāntātparaḥ prāṇā na hi kāntātparaḥ striyāḥ ..

4.17.m:
there is no life higher than the husband, nor anything beyond the husband for a woman.

4.17.m:
just as a mother's mind is on her only son, and the mind of lustful men is on women;
and the mind of misers is on wealth acquired over a long time;

4.17.s:
yathā bhayeṣu bhītānāṃ śāstreṣu viduṣāṃ yathā ..
stanādāne śiśūnāṃ ca śilpeṣu śilpināṃ yathā .. 92 ..
4.17.d:
यथा भयेषु भीतानां शास्त्रेषु विदुषां यथा ॥

4.17.m:

and of infants on taking the breast, and of artisans on arts;

4.17.s:
yathā jāre puṃścalīnāṃ sādhvīnāṃ ca tathā priye ..
taṃ vinā jīvituṃ brahmankṣaṇamekaṃ na ca kṣamam .. 93 ..
4.17.d:

4.17.m:
just as the mind of unchaste women is on a lover, so that of virtuous wives is on their beloved.
Without him, O Brahman, it is impossible to live even for a single moment.

4.17.s:
maraṇaṃ jīvanaṃ tāsāṃ jīvanaṃ maraṇādhikam ..

4.17.d:
मरणं जीवनं तासां जीवनं मरणाधिकम् ॥

अन्यशोकनिमग्नानां कालेन पानभोजनात् ॥ 94 ॥

4.17.s:
viparītaḥ kāntaśoko varddhate bhakṣaṇādaho ..

4.17.d:

4.17.m:
the opposite is grief for a husband—alas, it increases from eating!
A chaste wife follows like the shadow of her husband's deeds; among companions, a chaste wife is supreme.

4.17.s:
itare bhogadehānte sādhvī janmani janmani ..

4.17.m:
At the end of the body of experiences with others, the virtuous woman [remains his] in birth after birth.
If you, O Creator of the universe, make him liberated without me,

4.17.s:

हितं पीयूषसदृशं भयसंविग्नमानसः ॥ 97 ॥
4.17.m:
then having cursed you, O Lord, behold, I will lay the murder of a woman upon you!"
Hearing the speech of Kalāvatī, Brahmā, astonished
and with a mind agitated by fear, spoke words that were beneficial and nectar-like.

4.17.s:
brahmovāca .. ..

4.17.m: "Child, I will not give liberation to your husband without you.

4.17.s:
muktaṃ kartuṃ tvayā sārddhaṃ sāmprataṃ nāhamīśvaraḥ ..

4.17.m:

4.17.m:

Enjoy heavenly pleasure together with your husband for several years;

When Rādhikā herself will become your chaste daughter,

liberated while living, you two will go to Goloka together with her.

desire servitude to Hari, which is hard to obtain, and not [mere] cessation.

In time, having enjoyed their pleasures in Bhārata,

Remembering his past lives, a portion of Hari, like the moon in the bright fortnight,

4.17.m:
the lord of Vraja grew day by day there in the home of Vraja.
He was omniscient, a great yogin, with his mind set on Hari's lotus feet,

nandadabandhurvadānyaśca rūpavānguṇavānsudhīḥ ..

4.17.m:
a friend of Nanda, generous, handsome, virtuous, and wise.

4.17.m:
blazing with splendor, with the luster of refined gold.

In time, she became a beautiful maiden in the bloom of youth,

4.17.m:

gacchantī rājamārgeṇa gajendramandagāminī ..

4.17.m:

jitendriyaśca jñānī ca mūrcchāmāpa tathā'pi ca..
trasto lokānpathi gatāṃstūrṇaṃ papraccha sādaram..4.17.120..
4.17.d:
जितेन्द्रियश्च ज्ञानी च मूर्च्छामाप तथाऽपि च॥
त्रस्तो लोकान्पथि गतांस्तूर्णं पप्रच्छ सादरम्॥4.17.120॥
4.17.m:
Though he had conquered his senses and possessed knowledge, he nevertheless swooned.
Alarmed, he quickly and respectfully asked the people passing on the road:

4.17.s:
gacchantī kasya kanyeyamiti hovāca taṃ janaḥ ..
bhanandanasya nṛpateḥ kanyā nāmnā kalāvatī .. 121 ..
4.17.d:
गच्छन्ती कस्य कन्येयमिति होवाच तं जनः ॥
भनन्दनस्य नृपतेः कन्या नाम्ना कलावती ॥ 121 ॥
4.17.m:
“Whose daughter is this walking [here]?” The people replied to him:
“She is the daughter of King Bhanandana, named Kalāvatī,

4.17.s:
kamalākalayā dhanyā saṃbhūtā nṛpamandire ..
kautukena ca gacchantī krīḍārthaṃ sakhimandiram .. 122 ..
4.17.d:
कमलाकलया धन्या संभूता नृपमन्दिरे ॥
कौतुकेन च गच्छन्ती क्रीडार्थं सखिमन्दिरम् ॥ 122 ॥
4.17.m:
blessed, born by a part of Kamalā in the king's palace.
Curious, she is going to her friend's house for play.

4.17.s:
vraja vraja vrajaśreṣṭhetyuktvā loko jagāma ha ..
prahṛṣṭamānaso nando jagāma rājamandiram .. 123 ..
4.17.d:
व्रज व्रज व्रजश्रेष्ठेत्युक्त्वा लोको जगाम ह ॥
प्रहृष्टमानसो नन्दो जगाम राजमन्दिरम् ॥ 123 ॥
4.17.m:
Go, go, O best of Vraja!” Having spoken thus, the people went on.
With a delighted heart, Nanda went to the royal palace.

4.17.s:
avaruhya rathāttūrṇaṃ viveśa nṛpateḥ sabhām ..
utthāya rājā saṃbhāṣya svarṇasiṃhāsanaṃ dadau .. 124 ..
4.17.d:
अवरुह्य रथात्तूर्णं विवेश नृपतेः सभाम् ॥
उत्थाय राजा संभाष्य स्वर्णसिंहासनं ददौ ॥ 124 ॥
4.17.m:
Swiftly descending from his chariot, he entered the king's assembly.
Standing up and greeting him, the king offered him a golden throne.

4.17.s:
iṣṭālāpaṃ bahutaraṃ cakāra ca parasparam ..
vinayāvanato nandaḥ sambandhoktiṃ cakāra ha .. 125 ..
4.17.d:
इष्टालापं बहुतरं चकार च परस्परम् ॥
विनयावनतो नन्दः सम्बन्धोक्तिं चकार ह ॥ 125 ॥
4.17.m:
They engaged in much pleasant conversation with each other.
Bowed with humility, Nanda made a proposal of marriage.

4.17.s:
nanda uvāca ..
śṛṇu rājendra vakṣyāmi viśeṣavacanaṃ śubham ..
saṃbandhaṃ kuru kanyāyā viśiṣṭena ca sāmpratam .. 126 ..
4.17.d:
नन्द उवाच ॥
शृणु राजेन्द्र वक्ष्यामि विशेषवचनं शुभम् ॥
संबन्धं कुरु कन्याया विशिष्टेन च साम्प्रतम् ॥ 126 ॥
4.17.m:
“Listen, O best of kings, I shall speak an auspicious and particular word:
Arrange an alliance for your daughter now with a distinguished man.

4.17.s:
surabhānusutaḥ śrīmānvṛṣabhānurvrajādhipaḥ ..
nārāyaṇāṃśo guṇavānsundaraśca supaṇḍitaḥ .. 127 ..
4.17.d:
सुरभानुसुतः श्रीमान्वृषभानुर्व्रजाधिपः ॥
नारायणांशो गुणवान्सुन्दरश्च सुपण्डितः ॥ 127 ॥
4.17.m:
The glorious Vṛṣabhānu, lord of Vraja, is the son of Surabhānu.
He is a portion of Nārāyaṇa, virtuous, handsome, and deeply learned,

4.17.s:
sthirayauvanayuktaśca yogī jātismaro yuvā ..
kanyā te'yonisaṃbhūtā yajñakuṇḍasamudbhavā .. 128 ..
4.17.d:
स्थिरयौवनयुक्तश्च योगी जातिस्मरो युवा ॥
कन्या तेऽयोनिसंभूता यज्ञकुण्डसमुद्भवा ॥ 128 ॥
4.17.m:
endowed with eternal youth, a yogin, mindful of his past births, and young.
Your daughter is not born from a womb, but has arisen from a sacrificial pit;

4.17.s:
trailokyamohinī śāntā kamalāṃśā kalāvatī ..
sa ca yogyastvadduhitustadyogyā te ca kanyakā .. 129 ..
4.17.d:
त्रैलोक्यमोहिनी शान्ता कमलांशा कलावती ॥
स च योग्यस्त्वद्दुहितुस्तद्योग्या ते च कन्यका ॥ 129 ॥
4.17.m:
she is Kalāvatī, an enchantress of the three worlds, peaceful, a portion of Kamalā.
He is worthy of your daughter, and your daughter is worthy of him.

4.17.s:
vidagdhāyā vidagdhena saṃbandho guṇavānnṛpa ..
ityevamuktvā nandastu virarāma ca saṃsadi ..
uvāca taṃ nṛpaśreṣṭho vinayāvanato mune .. .. 4.17.130 ..
4.17.d:
विदग्धाया विदग्धेन संबन्धो गुणवान्नृप ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा नन्दस्तु विरराम च संसदि ॥
उवाच तं नृपश्रेष्ठो विनयावनतो मुने ॥ ॥ 4.17.130 ॥
4.17.m:
An alliance of an accomplished woman with an accomplished man is excellent, O King.”
Having spoken thus, Nanda fell silent in the assembly.
Bowed in humility, the best of kings said to him, O sage:

4.17.s:
bhanandana uvāca ..
saṃbandho hi vidhivaśo na me sādhyo vrajādhipa .. 131 ..
4.17.d:
भनन्दन उवाच ॥
संबन्धो हि विधिवशो न मे साध्यो व्रजाधिप ॥ 131 ॥
4.17.m: “An alliance is indeed under the power of destiny; it is not in my control, O lord of Vraja.”

4.17.s:
prajāpatiryogakartā janmadātā'hameva ca ..
kā kasya patnī kanyā vā varaḥ ko vā sasādhanaḥ .. 132 ..
4.17.d:
प्रजापतिर्योगकर्ता जन्मदाताऽहमेव च ॥
का कस्य पत्नी कन्या वा वरः को वा ससाधनः ॥ 132 ॥
4.17.m:
Brahma is the arranger of unions, and I am merely the giver of birth;
who is whose wife, or whose daughter, or who is the bridegroom endowed with means?

4.17.s:
karmānurūpaphaladaḥ sarveṣāṃ kāraṇaṃ vidhiḥ ..
bhavitavyaṃ kṛtaṃ karma tadamoghaṃ śrutau śrutam .. 133 ..
4.17.d:
कर्मानुरूपफलदः सर्वेषां कारणं विधिः ॥
भवितव्यं कृतं कर्म तदमोघं श्रुतौ श्रुतम् ॥ 133 ॥
4.17.m:
Fate, which grants fruits in accordance with past deeds, is the cause of all things.
What is destined will happen through action performed; that is unfailing, as heard in the Veda.

4.17.s:
anyathā niṣphalaṃ sarvamanīśasyodyamo yathā ..
vṛṣabhānupriyā dhātrā likhitā cetsutā mama .. .. 134 ..
4.17.d:
अन्यथा निष्फलं सर्वमनीशस्योद्यमो यथा ॥
वृषभानुप्रिया धात्रा लिखिता चेत्सुता मम ॥ ॥ 134 ॥
4.17.m:
Otherwise, everything is fruitless, just like the effort of a powerless person.
If my daughter has been written by the Creator as the beloved of Vṛṣabhānu,

4.17.s:
purā bhūtaiva ko vā'haṃ kenānyena nivāryate ..
ityevamuktvā rājendro vinayānatakaṃdharaḥ .. 135 ..
4.17.d:
पुरा भूतैव को वाऽहं केनान्येन निवार्यते ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा राजेन्द्रो विनयानतकंधरः ॥ 135 ॥
4.17.m:
it was already determined long ago; who am I, and by what other person could it be prevented?”
Having spoken thus, the king of kings, his neck bowed with humility,

4.17.s:
miṣṭānnaṃ bhojayāmāsa sādareṇa ca nārada ..
nṛpānujñāmupādāya vrajarājo vrajaṃ gataḥ .. 136 ..
4.17.d:
मिष्टान्नं भोजयामास सादरेण च नारद ॥
नृपानुज्ञामुपादाय व्रजराजो व्रजं गतः ॥ 136 ॥
4.17.m:
fed [him] sweetmeats with great respect, O Nārada.
Taking leave of the king, the king of Vraja returned to Vraja.

4.17.s:
gatvā sa kathayāmāsa surabhānasya saṃsadi ..
surabhānaśca yatnena nandanena ca sādaram .. 137 ..
4.17.d:
गत्वा स कथयामास सुरभानस्य संसदि ॥
सुरभानश्च यत्नेन नन्दनेन च सादरम् ॥ 137 ॥
4.17.m:
Having arrived, he related [it] in the assembly of Surabhānu.
And Surabhānu, with effort and respectfully together with Nanda,

4.17.s:
saṃbandhaṃ yojayāmāsa gargadvārā ca satvaram ..
vivāhakāle rājendro vipulaṃ yautakaṃ dadau .. .. 138 ..
4.17.d:
संबन्धं योजयामास गर्गद्वारा च सत्वरम् ॥
विवाहकाले राजेन्द्रो विपुलं यौतकं ददौ ॥ ॥ 138 ॥
4.17.m:
speedily arranged the marriage alliance through Garga.
At the time of the wedding, the king of kings gave an abundant dowry:

4.17.s:
gajaratnamaśvaratnaṃ ratnāni maṇibhūṣaṇam ..
vṛṣabhānurmudā yuktaḥ prāpya tāṃ ca kalāvatīm .. 139 ..
4.17.d:
गजरत्नमश्वरत्नं रत्नानि मणिभूषणम् ॥
वृषभानुर्मुदा युक्तः प्राप्य तां च कलावतीम् ॥ 139 ॥
4.17.m:
splendid elephants, splendid horses, jewels, and gemstone ornaments.
Filled with joy upon obtaining Kalāvatī,

4.17.s:
reme sunirjane ramye bubudhe na divāniśam ..
cakṣurnimeṣavirahādvyākulāṃ svāminā vinā .. 4.17.140 ..
4.17.d:
रेमे सुनिर्जने रम्ये बुबुधे न दिवानिशम् ॥
चक्षुर्निमेषविरहाद्व्याकुलां स्वामिना विना ॥ 4.17.140 ॥
4.17.m:
Vṛṣabhānu sported [with her] in a very secluded, charming place, unaware of day or night.
She became agitated even at the separation of the blink of an eye without her husband,

4.17.s:
vyākulo vṛṣabhānuśca kṣaṇena ca tayā vinā ..
jātismarā ca sā kanyā māyāmānuṣarūpiṇī .. 141 ..
4.17.d:
व्याकुलो वृषभानुश्च क्षणेन च तया विना ॥
जातिस्मरा च सा कन्या मायामानुषरूपिणी ॥ 141 ॥
4.17.m:
and Vṛṣabhānu was agitated in an instant without her.
That maiden, possessing memory of her past lives, had assumed the illusory form of a human,

4.17.s:
jātismaro hareraṃśo vṛṣabhāno mudā'nvitaḥ ..
vavṛdhe ca tayoḥ prema nityaṃnityaṃ navaṃnavam .. 142 ..
4.17.d:
जातिस्मरो हरेरंशो वृषभानो मुदाऽन्वितः ॥
ववृधे च तयोः प्रेम नित्यंनित्यं नवंनवम् ॥ 142 ॥
4.17.m:
and Vṛṣabhānu, a portion of Hari, also remembered his past lives, filled with joy.
Their love grew daily, ever fresh and new.

4.17.s:
sadā sakāmā sā prauḍhā sa ca kāmasamo yuvā ..
tayoḥ kanyā ca kālena rādhikā sā babhūva ha ..
daivātsudāma śāpena śrīkṛṣṇasyājñayā purā .. 143 ..
4.17.d:
सदा सकामा सा प्रौढा स च कामसमो युवा ॥
तयोः कन्या च कालेन राधिका सा बभूव ह ॥
दैवात्सुदाम शापेन श्रीकृष्णस्याज्ञया पुरा ॥ 143 ॥
4.17.m:
She was ever full of desire, fully mature, and he was a youth equal to Kāma.
In time, Rādhikā indeed became their daughter
by destiny, through the curse of Sudāman, by the command of Śrī Kṛṣṇa long ago.

4.17.s:
ayonisaṃbhavā sā ca kṛṣṇaprāṇādhikā satī ..
yasyā darśanamātreṇa tau vimuktau babhūvatuḥ.. .. 144 ..
4.17.d:
अयोनिसंभवा सा च कृष्णप्राणाधिका सती ॥
यस्या दर्शनमात्रेण तौ विमुक्तौ बभूवतुः॥ ॥ 144 ॥
4.17.m:
She, who was not born from a womb, was the virtuous woman dearer to Kṛṣṇa than life itself,
by the mere sight of whom both of them attained liberation.

4.17.s:
itihāsaśca kathitaḥ prakṛtaṃ śṛṇu sāmpratam ..
pāpendhanānāṃ dāhe ca jvaladagniśikhopamaḥ ...44...
4.17.d:
इतिहासश्च कथितः प्रकृतं शृणु साम्प्रतम् ॥
पापेन्धनानां दाहे च ज्वलदग्निशिखोपमः ॥.44॥।
4.17.m:
The traditional account has been told; now listen to the subject at hand,
which resembles a blaze of flaming fire in burning the fuel of sins.

4.17.s:
vṛṣabhānāśramaṃ gatvā śilpināṃ pravaro mudā ..
sthānāntaraṃ viśvakarmā jagāma svagaṇaiḥ saha .. 146 ..
4.17.d:
वृषभानाश्रमं गत्वा शिल्पिनां प्रवरो मुदा ॥
स्थानान्तरं विश्वकर्मा जगाम स्वगणैः सह ॥ 146 ॥
4.17.m:
Having gone to Vṛṣabhānu's hermitage, Viśvakarman, the best of craftsmen,
went joyfully with his attendants to another location.

4.17.s:
krośamātraṃ sthalaṃ cāru manasā''locya tattvavit ..
āśramaṃ kartumārebhe nandasya sumahātmanaḥ .. 147 ..
4.17.d:
क्रोशमात्रं स्थलं चारु मनसा'ऽलोच्य तत्त्ववित् ॥
आश्रमं कर्तुमारेभे नन्दस्य सुमहात्मनः ॥ 147 ॥
4.17.m:
After examining with his mind a charming site measuring a krośa, the knower of truth
began to construct the residence of the great-souled Nanda.

4.17.s:
kṛtvā'numānaṃ buddhyā ca sarvato'pi vilakṣaṇam ..
parikhābhirgabhīrābhiścaturbhiḥ saṃyutaṃ varam .. 148 ..
4.17.d:
कृत्वाऽनुमानं बुद्ध्या च सर्वतोऽपि विलक्षणम् ॥
परिखाभिर्गभीराभिश्चतुर्भिः संयुतं वरम् ॥ 148 ॥
4.17.m:
Having conceived it mentally, extraordinary in every respect,
an excellent [dwelling] enclosed by four deep moats,

4.17.s:
durlaṅghyābhirvairibhiśca khanitābhiśca prastaraiḥ ..
puṣyodyānaiḥ puṣpitābhiḥ pārāvāreṣu puṣpitaiḥ .. 149..
4.17.d:
दुर्लङ्घ्याभिर्वैरिभिश्च खनिताभिश्च प्रस्तरैः ॥
पुष्योद्यानैः पुष्पिताभिः पारावारेषु पुष्पितैः ॥ 149॥
4.17.m:
insurmountable to enemies and excavated with stones,
adorned on both banks with blossoming flower gardens,

4.17.s:
cāru campakavṛkṣaiśca puṣpitaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ ..
parito vāsitābhiśca sugandhivāyunā mune .. 4.17.150 ..
4.17.d:
चारु चम्पकवृक्षैश्च पुष्पितैः सुमनोहरैः ॥
परितो वासिताभिश्च सुगन्धिवायुना मुने ॥ 4.17.150 ॥
4.17.m:
and with lovely, delightful, flowering campaka trees,
fragrant all around with sweet-smelling wind, O sage,

4.17.s:
āmrairguḍālaiḥ panasaiḥ kharjūrairnārikelakaiḥ ..
dāḍimaiḥ śrīphalairbhṛṅgairjambīrairnāgaraṅgakaiḥ ..151..
4.17.d:
आम्रैर्गुडालैः पनसैः खर्जूरैर्नारिकेलकैः ॥
दाडिमैः श्रीफलैर्भृङ्गैर्जम्बीरैर्नागरङ्गकैः ॥151॥
4.17.m:
with mangoes, guḍālas, jackfruits, dates, coconuts,
pomegranates, bilvas, bhṛṅgas, citrons, oranges,

4.17.s:
tuṅgairāmrātakairjambusamūhaiśca phalānvitaiḥ ..
kadalīnāṃ ketakīnāṃ kadambānāṃ kadambakaiḥ .. .. 152 ..
4.17.d:
तुङ्गैराम्रातकैर्जम्बुसमूहैश्च फलान्वितैः ॥
कदलीनां केतकीनां कदम्बानां कदम्बकैः ॥ ॥ 152 ॥
4.17.m:
lofty āmrātakas, clusters of rose-apples laden with fruit,
and groves of plantains, ketakīs, and kadambas;

4.17.s:
sarvataḥ śobhitābhiśca phalaistaiḥ puṣpitairaho ..
krīḍārhābhirnigūḍhābhirvāñchitābhiśca sarvadā .. 153 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वतः शोभिताभिश्च फलैस्तैः पुष्पितैरहो ॥
क्रीडार्हाभिर्निगूढाभिर्वाञ्छिताभिश्च सर्वदा ॥ 153 ॥
4.17.m:
beautified on all sides, oh, by those fruits and flowers,
suitable for sport, secret, and always desirable.

4.17.s:
parikhānāṃ rahaḥ sthāne cakāra mārgamuttamam ..
durgamaṃ paravargāṇāṃ svānāṃ ca sugamaṃ sadā .. 154 ..
4.17.d:
परिखानां रहः स्थाने चकार मार्गमुत्तमम् ॥
दुर्गमं परवर्गाणां स्वानां च सुगमं सदा ॥ 154 ॥
4.17.m:
In a secluded place along the moats, he made an excellent path,
difficult of access to enemies and always easily traversed by their own people,

4.17.s:
saṃketena maṇistambhaiśchāditaiḥ svalpapāthasā ..
stambhasīmākṛtamaho na saṃkīrṇaṃ na vistṛtam .. 159 ..
4.17.d:
संकेतेन मणिस्तम्भैश्छादितैः स्वल्पपाथसा ॥
स्तम्भसीमाकृतमहो न संकीर्णं न विस्तृतम् ॥ 159 ॥
4.17.m:
marked secretly by gem-encrusted pillars covered with shallow water;
bounded by pillars, oh, neither narrow nor wide.

4.17.s:
parikhoparibhāge ca prākāraṃ sumanoharam ..
dhanuḥśatapramāṇaṃ ca cakārātisamucchritam .. 156 ..
4.17.d:
परिखोपरिभागे च प्राकारं सुमनोहरम् ॥
धनुःशतप्रमाणं च चकारातिसमुच्छ्रितम् ॥ 156 ॥
4.17.m:
And on the upper part of the moat, he made a very enchanting rampart,
measuring a hundred bows and exceedingly lofty.

4.17.s:
prastarasya pramāṇaṃ ca pañcaviṃśatihastakam ..
sindūrākāramaṇibhirnirmitaṃ cātisundaram .. 157 ..
4.17.d:
प्रस्तरस्य प्रमाणं च पञ्चविंशतिहस्तकम् ॥
सिन्दूराकारमणिभिर्निर्मितं चातिसुन्दरम् ॥ 157 ॥
4.17.m:
The size of each stone was twenty-five cubits,
and it was constructed very beautifully with gems the color of vermilion.

4.17.s:
bāhye dvābhyāṃ ca saṃyuktamantare saptabhistathā ..
dvārbhiśca sanniruddhābhirmaṇisārakapāṭakaiḥ ..158..
4.17.d:
बाह्ये द्वाभ्यां च संयुक्तमन्तरे सप्तभिस्तथा ॥
द्वार्भिश्च सन्निरुद्धाभिर्मणिसारकपाटकैः ॥158॥
4.17.m:
It was furnished with two [gates] on the outside and likewise seven on the inside,
with gates barred by panels made of the finest gems,

4.17.s:
harinmaṇīnāṃ kalaśaiścitrayuktairvirājitam ..
maṇisāravikāraiśca kapāṭaiśca suśobhitam .. 159 ..
4.17.d:
हरिन्मणीनां कलशैश्चित्रयुक्तैर्विराजितम् ॥
मणिसारविकारैश्च कपाटैश्च सुशोभितम् ॥ 159 ॥
4.17.m:
shining with emerald finials adorned with varied designs,
and splendidly decorated with doors formed of the finest jewels;

4.17.s:
svarṇasāravinirmāṇakalaśojjvalaśekharam ..
nandālayaṃ vinirmāya babhrāma nagaraṃ punaḥ .. 4.17.160 ..
4.17.d:
स्वर्णसारविनिर्माणकलशोज्ज्वलशेखरम् ॥
नन्दालयं विनिर्माय बभ्राम नगरं पुनः ॥ 4.17.160 ॥
4.17.m:
having radiant spires with pitchers made of the finest gold.
Having constructed Nanda's residence, he traversed the settlement again,

4.17.s:
rājamārgāśca vividhānsa ca cārūṃścakāra ha ..
raktabhānuvikāraiśca vedībhiśca supattanaiḥ .. 161 ..
4.17.d:
राजमार्गाश्च विविधान्स च चारूंश्चकार ह ॥
रक्तभानुविकारैश्च वेदीभिश्च सुपत्तनैः ॥ 161 ॥
4.17.m:
and made various beautiful highways.
[adorned] with structures fashioned from red sunstone, and platforms with splendid sites,

4.17.s:
pārāvāre ca parito nibandhāṃśca manoharān ..
vāṇijyārhaiśca vaṇijāṃ parito maṇimaṇḍapaiḥ .. 162 ..
4.17.d:
पारावारे च परितो निबन्धांश्च मनोहरान् ॥
वाणिज्यार्हैश्च वणिजां परितो मणिमण्डपैः ॥ 162 ॥
4.17.m:
and on both banks around, delightful embankments,
and with jewelled pavilions suitable for merchants' commerce on every side,

4.17.s:
sarvato dakṣiṇe vāme jvaladbhiśca virājitān ..
tato vṛndāvanaṃ gatvā nirmame rāsamaṇḍalam..163..
4.17.d:
सर्वतो दक्षिणे वामे ज्वलद्भिश्च विराजितान् ॥
ततो वृन्दावनं गत्वा निर्ममे रासमण्डलम्॥163॥
4.17.m:
adorned with blazing [lights] on all sides, to the right and to the left.
Then, having gone to Vṛndāvana, he created the circular arena for the rāsa dance:

4.17.s:
sundaraṃ maṇḍalākāraṃ maṇiprākārasaṃyutam ..
parito yojanāyāmaṃ maṇivedibhiranvitam .. 164 ..
4.17.d:
सुन्दरं मण्डलाकारं मणिप्राकारसंयुतम् ॥
परितो योजनायामं मणिवेदिभिरन्वितम् ॥ 164 ॥
4.17.m:
beautiful, circular in form, endowed with an enclosure of gems,
extending one yojana all around, furnished with jewelled dais-platforms,

4.17.s:
maṇisāravikāraiśca maṇḍapairnavakoṭibhiḥ ..
śṛṅgārārhaiśca citrāḍhyai ratitalpasamanvitaiḥ .. 165 ..
4.17.d:
मणिसारविकारैश्च मण्डपैर्नवकोटिभिः ॥
शृङ्गारार्हैश्च चित्राढ्यै रतितल्पसमन्वितैः ॥ 165 ॥
4.17.m:
and with ninety million pavilions fashioned from the finest gems,
suited for amorous play, richly painted, furnished with couches for lovemaking,

4.17.s:
nānājātiprasūnānāṃ vāyunā surabhīkṛtaiḥ ..
ratnapradīpasaṃyuktaiḥ suvarṇakalaśojjvalaiḥ .. 166 ..
4.17.d:
नानाजातिप्रसूनानां वायुना सुरभीकृतैः ॥
रत्नप्रदीपसंयुक्तैः सुवर्णकलशोज्ज्वलैः ॥ 166 ॥
4.17.m:
made fragrant by the breeze of flowers of various kinds,
endowed with jewelled lamps, bright with golden pitchers,

4.17.s:
puṣpodyānaiḥ puṣpitaiśca sarobhiśca suśobhitam ..
rāsasthalaṃ vinirmāya jagāmānyatsthalaṃ puraḥ .. 167 ..
4.17.d:
पुष्पोद्यानैः पुष्पितैश्च सरोभिश्च सुशोभितम् ॥
रासस्थलं विनिर्माय जगामान्यत्स्थलं पुरः ॥ 167 ॥
4.17.m:
[and] richly adorned with blooming flower gardens and lakes.
Having fashioned the place of the rāsa dance, he went further ahead to another location.

4.17.s:
dṛṣṭvā vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ parituṣṭo babhūva ha ..
vṛndāvanābhyantare ca sthānesthāne sunirjane .. 168 ..
4.17.d:
दृष्ट्वा वृन्दावनं रम्यं परितुष्टो बभूव ह ॥
वृन्दावनाभ्यन्तरे च स्थानेस्थाने सुनिर्जने ॥ 168 ॥
4.17.m:
Seeing delightful Vṛndāvana, he was exceedingly pleased.
And inside Vṛndāvana, in various places that were very secluded,

4.17.s:
kṛtvā parimitaṃ buddhyā manasālocya yatnataḥ ..
vilakṣaṇāni ramyāṇi tatra triṃśadvanāni ca .. 169 ..
4.17.d:
कृत्वा परिमितं बुद्ध्या मनसालोच्य यत्नतः ॥
विलक्षणानि रम्याणि तत्र त्रिंशद्वनानि च ॥ 169 ॥
4.17.m:
having measured with his intellect and reflected in his mind with care,
thirty extraordinary and delightful groves there

4.17.s:
rādhāmādhavayoreva krīḍārthaṃ ca vinirmame ..
tato madhuvanābhyāśe nirjane'timanohare .. 4.17.170..
4.17.d:
राधामाधवयोरेव क्रीडार्थं च विनिर्ममे ॥
ततो मधुवनाभ्याशे निर्जनेऽतिमनोहरे ॥ 4.17.170॥
4.17.m:
he fashioned for the sporting of Rādhā and Mādhava.
Then, near Madhuvana, in a secluded and very captivating spot,

4.17.s:
vaṭamūlasamīpe ca sarasaḥ paścime taṭe ..
campakodyānapūrvāyāṃ ketakīvanamadhyataḥ ..171..
4.17.d:
वटमूलसमीपे च सरसः पश्चिमे तटे ॥
चम्पकोद्यानपूर्वायां केतकीवनमध्यतः ॥171॥
4.17.m:
near the foot of a banyan tree, on the western bank of a lake,
to the east of a campaka garden, in the midst of a ketakī forest,

4.17.s:
punastayośca krīḍārthaṃ cakāra ratnamaṇḍapam ..
caturbhirvedikābhiśca parītamatisundaram ..172..
4.17.d:
पुनस्तयोश्च क्रीडार्थं चकार रत्नमण्डपम् ॥
चतुर्भिर्वेदिकाभिश्च परीतमतिसुन्दरम् ॥172॥
4.17.m:
again for their sporting, he made a jewelled pavilion,
surrounded by four daises, exceedingly beautiful,

4.17.s:
sadratnasāraracitai rājitaṃ tūlikāśataiḥ ..
amūlyaratnaracitairnānācitreṇa citritaiḥ..173..
4.17.d:
सद्रत्नसाररचितै राजितं तूलिकाशतैः ॥
अमूल्यरत्नरचितैर्नानाचित्रेण चित्रितैः॥173॥
4.17.m:
shining with hundreds of mattresses crafted of the essence of fine gems,
fashioned with priceless gems and decorated with various paintings,

4.17.s:
kapāṭairnavabhiryuktaṃ navadvārairmanoharaiḥ ..
ratneṃdracittrakalaśaiḥ kṛtrimaiśca trikoṭibhiḥ .. 174 ..
4.17.d:
कपाटैर्नवभिर्युक्तं नवद्वारैर्मनोहरैः ॥
रत्नेंद्रचित्त्रकलशैः कृत्रिमैश्च त्रिकोटिभिः ॥ 174 ॥
4.17.m:
equipped with nine panels and nine delightful doors,
with thirty million decorative and artfully fashioned pitchers of topaz,

4.17.s:
paritaḥ parito bhittyāmūrdhvaṃ ca pariśobhitam ..
mahāmaṇīndravikṛtairārohairnavabhirvṛtam ..175..
4.17.d:
परितः परितो भित्त्यामूर्ध्वं च परिशोभितम् ॥
महामणीन्द्रविकृतैरारोहैर्नवभिर्वृतम् ॥175॥
4.17.m:
beautified all around on the walls and up above,
furnished with nine flights of stairs made of great, precious gems,

4.17.s:
sadratnasāraracitakalaśojjvalaśekharam..
patākātoraṇairyuktaṃ śobhitaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ ..176..
4.17.d:
सद्रत्नसाररचितकलशोज्ज्वलशेखरम्॥
पताकातोरणैर्युक्तं शोभितं श्वेतचामरैः ॥176॥
4.17.m:
its crest radiant with pitchers fashioned from the finest gems,
equipped with banners and archways, and adorned with white fly-whisks,

4.17.s:
sarvataḥ purato dīptamamūlyaratna darpaṇaiḥ ..
dhanuḥpramāṇaśatakamūrdhvamagniśikhopamam ..177..
4.17.d:
सर्वतः पुरतो दीप्तममूल्यरत्न दर्पणैः ॥
धनुःप्रमाणशतकमूर्ध्वमग्निशिखोपमम् ॥177॥
4.17.m:
blazing everywhere before it with mirrors of priceless gems,
a hundred bow-lengths high, resembling a flame of fire,

4.17.s:
śatahastapramāṇaṃ ca prastāraṃ vartulākṛtim ..
śobhitaṃ ratnakalpaiśca tadabhyantaramuttamam ..178..
4.17.d:
शतहस्तप्रमाणं च प्रस्तारं वर्तुलाकृतिम् ॥
शोभितं रत्नकल्पैश्च तदभ्यन्तरमुत्तमम् ॥178॥
4.17.m:
a hundred cubits wide and circular in form;
and its excellent interior was decorated with gem-like ornaments,

4.17.s:
vahniśuddhāṃśukairvastrairmālājālavicitritaiḥ..
pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālyopadhānasaṃyutaiḥ..179..
4.17.d:
वह्निशुद्धांशुकैर्वस्त्रैर्मालाजालविचित्रितैः॥
पारिजातप्रसूनानां माल्योपधानसंयुतैः॥179॥
4.17.m:
with garments of fire-purified silk adorned with rows of garlands,
supplied with wreaths and cushions of pārijāta blossoms,

4.17.s:
candanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumaiḥ surabhīkṛtam ..
navaśṛṅgārayogyaiśca kāmavarddhanakāribhiḥ .. 4.17.180 ..
4.17.d:
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीकुङ्कुमैः सुरभीकृतम् ॥
नवशृङ्गारयोग्यैश्च कामवर्द्धनकारिभिः ॥ 4.17.180 ॥
4.17.m:
fragrant with sandalwood, aloe, musk, and saffron,
suitable for fresh erotic passion, exciting desire,

4.17.s:
mālatīcampakānāṃ ca puṣparājibhiranvitam ..
sakarpūraiśca tāmbūlaiḥ sadratnapātrasaṃsthitaiḥ .. 181 ..
4.17.d:
मालतीचम्पकानां च पुष्पराजिभिरन्वितम् ॥
सकर्पूरैश्च ताम्बूलैः सद्रत्नपात्रसंस्थितैः ॥ 181 ॥
4.17.m:
supplied with rows of flowers of mālatī and campaka,
with camphorated betel placed in fine vessels of gems,

4.17.s:
vajrasāreṇa khacitairmuktājālavilambibhiḥ ..
ratnasāraghaṭākīrṇaṃ ratnapīṭhaiḥ susaṃyutam .. 182 ..
4.17.d:
वज्रसारेण खचितैर्मुक्ताजालविलम्बिभिः ॥
रत्नसारघटाकीर्णं रत्नपीठैः सुसंयुतम् ॥ 182 ॥
4.17.m:
inlaid with the essence of diamond, hung with nets of pearls,
filled with jars made of precious gems, well furnished with jewelled pedestals,

4.17.s:
ratnasiṃhāsanairyuktaṃ ratnacitreṇa citritaiḥ ..
kṣaritaiścandrakāntaiśca susiktaṃ jalabindubhiḥ..183..
4.17.d:
रत्नसिंहासनैर्युक्तं रत्नचित्रेण चित्रितैः ॥
क्षरितैश्चन्द्रकान्तैश्च सुसिक्तं जलबिन्दुभिः॥183॥
4.17.m:
endowed with jewelled thrones decorated with depictions in gems,
well-sprinkled with drops of water exuded from moonstones,

4.17.s:
śītavāsitatoyena saṃyuktaṃ bhogavastubhiḥ ..
kṛtvā ratigṛhaṃ ramyaṃ nagaraṃ ca punaryayau .. 184 ..
4.17.d:
शीतवासिततोयेन संयुक्तं भोगवस्तुभिः ॥
कृत्वा रतिगृहं रम्यं नगरं च पुनर्ययौ ॥ 184 ॥
4.17.m:
with cool, perfumed water, and filled with articles of enjoyment.
Having fashioned this delightful pleasure-house, he returned to the settlement.

4.17.s:
yāni yeṣāṃ mandirāṇi tannāmāni lilekha saḥ ..
mudā yukto viśvakarmā śiṣyairyakṣagaṇaiḥ saha .. 185 ..
4.17.d:
यानि येषां मन्दिराणि तन्नामानि लिलेख सः ॥
मुदा युक्तो विश्वकर्मा शिष्यैर्यक्षगणैः सह ॥ 185 ॥
4.17.m:
Whichever houses belonged to whom, their names he inscribed.
Filled with joy, Viśvakarman, together with his disciples, the host of Yakṣas,

4.17.s:
nidreśaṃ nidritaṃ natvā prayayau svālayaṃ mune ..
sarvatraivaṃ sukṛtināṃ samastaṃ bhagavatkṛpā .. 186 ..
4.17.d:
निद्रेशं निद्रितं नत्वा प्रययौ स्वालयं मुने ॥
सर्वत्रैवं सुकृतिनां समस्तं भगवत्कृपा ॥ 186 ॥
4.17.m:
bowed to the sleeping lord of sleep and departed to his own abode, O sage.
Thus everywhere for the meritorious, everything is the grace of the Lord;

4.17.s:
nehāścaryaṃ ca nagaraṃ babhūveśecchayā bhuvi ..
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ hareścaritamaṅgalam ..
sukhadaṃ pātakaharaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 187 ..
4.17.d:
नेहाश्चर्यं च नगरं बभूवेशेच्छया भुवि ॥
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं हरेश्चरितमङ्गलम् ॥
सुखदं पातकहरं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 187 ॥
4.17.m:
nor was it a wonder that a city came to be on earth by the will of the Lord.
bestowing happiness and removing sin. What more do you wish to hear?

4.17.s:
.. nārada uvāca ..
kathaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ nāma kānanasyāsya bhārate ..
vyutpattirasya saṃjñā vā tattvaṃ vada sutattvavit .. 188 ..
4.17.d:
॥ नारद उवाच ॥
कथं वृन्दावनं नाम काननस्यास्य भारते ॥
व्युत्पत्तिरस्य संज्ञा वा तत्त्वं वद सुतत्त्ववित् ॥ 188 ॥
4.17.m:
Why is this forest in Bhārata called by the name of Vṛndāvana?
Tell me its etymology, its designation, and the truth of it, O knower of the highest truth!

4.17.s:
sūta uvāca ..
nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣirnārāyaṇo mudā ..
prahasyovāca nikhilaṃ tattvameva purātanam .. 189 ..
4.17.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषिर्नारायणो मुदा ॥
प्रहस्योवाच निखिलं तत्त्वमेव पुरातनम् ॥ 189 ॥
4.17.m:
Hearing the words of Nārada, the sage Nārāyaṇa, filled with joy,
smiled and spoke all the ancient truth.

4.17.s:
.. nārāyaṇa uvāca .. ..
purā kedāranṛpatiḥ saptadvīpapatiḥ svayam .. 4.17.190 ..
4.17.d:
॥ नारायण उवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा केदारनृपतिः सप्तद्वीपपतिः स्वयम् ॥ 4.17.190 ॥
4.17.m: Long ago, King Kedāra himself, ruler of the seven continents,

4.17.s:
āsītsatyayuge brahmansatyadharmarataḥ sadā ..
sa reme saha nārībhiḥ putrapautragaṇaiḥ saha .. 191 ..
4.17.d:
आसीत्सत्ययुगे ब्रह्मन्सत्यधर्मरतः सदा ॥
स रेमे सह नारीभिः पुत्रपौत्रगणैः सह ॥ 191 ॥
4.17.m:
lived in the Kṛtayuga, O Brahman, always devoted to the eternal law of truth.
He took pleasure with his women, along with hosts of sons and grandsons;

4.17.s:
putrāniva prajāḥ sarvāḥ pālayāmāsa dhārmikaḥ ..
kṛtvā kratuśataṃ rājā lebhe nendratvamīpsitam .. 192 ..
4.17.d:
पुत्रानिव प्रजाः सर्वाः पालयामास धार्मिकः ॥
कृत्वा क्रतुशतं राजा लेभे नेन्द्रत्वमीप्सितम् ॥ 192 ॥
4.17.m:
the righteous king protected all his subjects like sons.
Having performed a hundred sacrifices, the king did not desire Indra's status;

4.17.s:
kṛtvā nānāvidhaṃ puṇyaṃ phalakāṅkṣī na ca svayam ..
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ sarvaṃ śrīkṛṣṇaprītipūrvakam .. 193 ..
4.17.d:
कृत्वा नानाविधं पुण्यं फलकाङ्क्षी न च स्वयम् ॥
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं सर्वं श्रीकृष्णप्रीतिपूर्वकम् ॥ 193 ॥
4.17.m:
having performed various meritorious deeds, he personally did not crave rewards.
Every regular and occasional rite [he did] out of love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

4.17.s:
kedāratulyo rājendro na bhūto bhavitā punaḥ ..
putreṣu rājyaṃ saṃnyasya priyāṃ trailokyamohinīm .. 194 ..
4.17.d:
केदारतुल्यो राजेन्द्रो न भूतो भविता पुनः ॥
पुत्रेषु राज्यं संन्यस्य प्रियां त्रैलोक्यमोहिनीम् ॥ 194 ॥
4.17.m:
A royal sovereign equal to Kedāra has never been, nor will there ever be again.
Having handed over the kingdom and his wife, who enchanted the three worlds, to his sons,

4.17.s:
jaigīṣavyopadeśena jagāma tapase vanam ..
hareraikāntiko bhakto dhyāyate saṃtataṃ harim ..195..
4.17.d:
जैगीषव्योपदेशेन जगाम तपसे वनम् ॥
हरेरैकान्तिको भक्तो ध्यायते संततं हरिम् ॥195॥
4.17.m:
he went to the forest for austerities by the counsel of Jaigīṣavya.
An exclusive devotee of Hari, he constantly meditated on Hari.

4.17.s:
śaśvatsudarśanaṃ cakramasti yatsannidhau mune ..
ciraṃ taptvā muniśreṣṭho golokaṃ ca jagāma saḥ ..196 ..
4.17.d:
शश्वत्सुदर्शनं चक्रमस्ति यत्सन्निधौ मुने ॥
चिरं तप्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठो गोलोकं च जगाम सः ॥196 ॥
4.17.m:
The Sudarśana discus was perpetually in his presence, O sage.
Having performed austerities for a long time, that best of sages went to Goloka.

4.17.s:
kedāraṃ nāma tīrthaṃ ca tannāmnā ca babhūva ha ..
tatrādyāpi mṛtaḥ prāṇī sadyo mukto bhaveddhruvam .. 197 ..
4.17.d:
केदारं नाम तीर्थं च तन्नाम्ना च बभूव ह ॥
तत्राद्यापि मृतः प्राणी सद्यो मुक्तो भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 197 ॥
4.17.m:
The sacred place named Kedāra came into being by his name;
a living being who dies there even today certainly attains liberation instantly.

4.17.s:
kamalāṃśā tasya kanyā nāmnā vṛndā tapasvinī ..
na vavre sā varaṃ kaṃcidyogaśāstraviśāradā .. 198 ..
4.17.d:
कमलांशा तस्य कन्या नाम्ना वृन्दा तपस्विनी ॥
न वव्रे सा वरं कंचिद्योगशास्त्रविशारदा ॥ 198 ॥
4.17.m:
His daughter, a portion of Kamalā, was an ascetic named Vṛndā;
she, learned in the treatises on yoga, chose no husband at all.

4.17.s:
datto durvāsasā tasyai harermantraḥ sudurlabhaḥ ..
sā viraktā gṛhaṃ tyaktvā jagāma tapase vanam .. 199 ..
4.17.d:
दत्तो दुर्वाससा तस्यै हरेर्मन्त्रः सुदुर्लभः ॥
सा विरक्ता गृहं त्यक्त्वा जगाम तपसे वनम् ॥ 199 ॥
4.17.m:
The most rare mantra of Hari was given to her by Durvāsas;
detached, she abandoned home and went to the forest for austerities.

4.17.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi tapastepe sunirjane ..
āvirbabhūva śrīkṛṣṇastatpuro bhaktavatsalaḥ .. 4.17.200 ..
4.17.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तेपे सुनिर्जने ॥
आविर्बभूव श्रीकृष्णस्तत्पुरो भक्तवत्सलः ॥ 4.17.200 ॥
4.17.m:
She practiced severe austerities in complete solitude for sixty thousand years;
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, fond of his devotees, appeared before her.

4.17.s:
prasannavadanaḥ śrīmānvaraṃ vṛṇvityuvāca saḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā sā rādhikā kāntaṃ śānte sundaravigraham .. 201 ..
4.17.d:
प्रसन्नवदनः श्रीमान्वरं वृण्वित्युवाच सः ॥
दृष्ट्वा सा राधिका कान्तं शान्ते सुन्दरविग्रहम् ॥ 201 ॥
4.17.m:
With a pleased countenance, the glorious Lord said: "Choose a boon!"
Having seen Rādhikā's beloved, peaceful, with a handsome form,

4.17.s:
mūrcchāṃ saṃprāpa sā sadyaḥ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā ..
sā ca śīghraṃ varaṃ vavre patistvaṃ me bhaveti ca .. 202 ..
4.17.d:
मूर्च्छां संप्राप सा सद्यः कामबाणप्रपीडिता ॥
सा च शीघ्रं वरं वव्रे पतिस्त्वं मे भवेति च ॥ 202 ॥
4.17.m:
she immediately fell into a swoon, afflicted by Kāma's arrows.
She quickly chose the boon: "Become my husband!"

4.17.s:
omityuktvā ca rahasi ciraṃ reme tayā saha ..
sā jagāma ca golokaṃ kṛṣṇena saha kautukāt .. 203 ..
4.17.d:
ओमित्युक्त्वा च रहसि चिरं रेमे तया सह ॥
सा जगाम च गोलोकं कृष्णेन सह कौतुकात् ॥ 203 ॥
4.17.m:
Having said, "Om," he enjoyed pleasure with her in secret for a long time;
and she went to Goloka joyfully together with Kṛṣṇa.

4.17.s:
rādhā samā sā saubhāgyādgopīśreṣṭhā babhūva ha ..
vṛndā yatra tapastepe tattu vṛndāvanaṃ smṛtam .. 204 ..
4.17.d:
राधा समा सा सौभाग्याद्गोपीश्रेष्ठा बभूव ह ॥
वृन्दा यत्र तपस्तेपे तत्तु वृन्दावनं स्मृतम् ॥ 204 ॥
4.17.m:
Equal to Rādhā through good fortune, she became the best of the gopīs.
Where Vṛndā performed austerities is remembered as Vṛndāvana;

4.17.s:
vṛndayā'tra kṛtā krīḍā tena vā munipuṃgava ..
athā'nyaṃ cetihāsaṃ ca śṛṇuṣva vatsa puṇyadam .. 205 ..
4.17.d:
वृन्दयाऽत्र कृता क्रीडा तेन वा मुनिपुंगव ॥
अथाऽन्यं चेतिहासं च शृणुष्व वत्स पुण्यदम् ॥ 205 ॥
4.17.m:
or, O best of sages, because sporting was done here by Vṛndā.
Now listen to another sacred history, my child,

4.17.s:
yena vṛndāvanaṃ nāma nibodha kathayāmi te ..
kuśadhvajasya kanye dve dharmaśāstraviśārade .. 206 ..
4.17.d:
येन वृन्दावनं नाम निबोध कथयामि ते ॥
कुशध्वजस्य कन्ये द्वे धर्मशास्त्रविशारदे ॥ 206 ॥
4.17.m:
by which the name is Vṛndāvana; understand, I shall tell you.
Kuśadhvaja had two daughters skilled in the treatises on dharma,

4.17.s:
tulasīvedavatyau ca virakte bhavakarmaṇi ..
tapastaptvā vedavatī prāpa nārāyaṇaṃ param .. 207 ..
4.17.d:
तुलसीवेदवत्यौ च विरक्ते भवकर्मणि ॥
तपस्तप्त्वा वेदवती प्राप नारायणं परम् ॥ 207 ॥
4.17.m:
Tulasī and Vedavatī, detached from worldly action.
Having performed austerities, Vedavatī obtained supreme Nārāyaṇa;

4.17.s:
sītā janakakanyā sā sarvatra parikīrtitā ..
tulasī ca tapastaptvā vāñchāṃ kṛtvā hariṃ prati .. 206 ..
4.17.d:
सीता जनककन्या सा सर्वत्र परिकीर्तिता ॥
तुलसी च तपस्तप्त्वा वाञ्छां कृत्वा हरिं प्रति ॥ 206 ॥
4.17.m:
she is renowned everywhere as Sītā, daughter of Janaka.
And Tulasī, having performed austerities, harboring a desire for Hari,

4.17.s:
daivāddurvāsasaḥ śāpātprāpya śaṅkhāsuraṃ prati ..
paścātsaṃprāpya kamalākāntaṃ kāntaṃ manoharam .. 209 ..
4.17.d:
दैवाद्दुर्वाससः शापात्प्राप्य शङ्खासुरं प्रति ॥
पश्चात्संप्राप्य कमलाकान्तं कान्तं मनोहरम् ॥ 209 ॥
4.17.m:
obtained the demon Śaṅkha as husband by fate through the curse of Durvāsas;
afterward, having obtained the charming beloved, the lord of Kamalā,

4.17.s:
sā caiva hariśāpena vṛkṣarūpā sureśvarī ..
tasyāḥ śāpena ca hariḥ śālagrāmo babhūva ha .. 4.17.210 ..
4.17.d:
सा चैव हरिशापेन वृक्षरूपा सुरेश्वरी ॥
तस्याः शापेन च हरिः शालग्रामो बभूव ह ॥ 4.17.210 ॥
4.17.m:
that queen of deities took the form of a plant through Hari's curse;
and by her curse, Hari became the Śālagrāma [stone].

4.17.s:
tathā tasthau ca satataṃ śilāvakṣasi suṃdarī ..
vistīrṇaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tulasīcaritaṃ ca te ..
tathā'pi ca prasaṃgena kiṃciduktaṃ mune punaḥ .. 211 ..
4.17.d:
तथा तस्थौ च सततं शिलावक्षसि सुंदरी ॥
विस्तीर्णं कथितं सर्वं तुलसीचरितं च ते ॥
तथाऽपि च प्रसंगेन किंचिदुक्तं मुने पुनः ॥ 211 ॥

4.17.s:
tasyāśca tapasaḥ sthānaṃ tadidaṃ ca tapodhana ..
tena vṛndāvanaṃ nāma pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ .. 212 ..
4.17.d:
तस्याश्च तपसः स्थानं तदिदं च तपोधन ॥
तेन वृन्दावनं नाम प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ 212 ॥
4.17.m:
And this was the place of her austerities, O you rich in asceticism;
therefore the wise call it by the name Vṛndāvana.

4.17.s:
atha vā te pravakṣyāmi paraṃ hetvantaraṃ śṛṇu ..
yena vṛndāvanaṃ nāma puṇyakṣetrasya bhārate .. 213 ..
4.17.d:
अथ वा ते प्रवक्ष्यामि परं हेत्वन्तरं शृणु ॥
येन वृन्दावनं नाम पुण्यक्षेत्रस्य भारते ॥ 213 ॥
4.17.m:
Or I shall tell you another supreme reason; listen,
by which the holy site in Bhārata is named Vṛndāvana.

4.17.s:
rādhāṣoḍaśanāmnāṃ ca vṛndānāma śrutau śrutam ..
tasyāḥ krīḍāvanaṃ ramyaṃ tena vṛndāvanaṃ smṛtam .. 214 ..
4.17.d:
राधाषोडशनाम्नां च वृन्दानाम श्रुतौ श्रुतम् ॥
तस्याः क्रीडावनं रम्यं तेन वृन्दावनं स्मृतम् ॥ 214 ॥
4.17.m:
Among the sixteen names of Rādhā, the name Vṛndā is heard in the scriptures;
it was her charming pleasure-forest; therefore it is remembered as Vṛndāvana.

4.17.s:
goloke prītaye tasyāḥ kṛṣṇena nirmitaṃ purā ..
krīḍārthaṃ bhuvi tannāmnā vanaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ smṛtam .. 215 ..
4.17.d:
गोलोके प्रीतये तस्याः कृष्णेन निर्मितं पुरा ॥
क्रीडार्थं भुवि तन्नाम्ना वनं वृन्दावनं स्मृतम् ॥ 215 ॥
4.17.m:
Long ago, it was created by Kṛṣṇa in Goloka for her delight;
on earth, the forest is remembered as Vṛndāvana by that name for the purpose of sport.

4.17.s:
nārada uvāca ..
kāni ṣoḍaśa nāmāni rādhikāyā jagadguro ..
tāni me vada śiṣyāya śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama .. 216 ..
4.17.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
कानि षोडश नामानि राधिकाया जगद्गुरो ॥
तानि मे वद शिष्याय श्रोतुं कौतूहलं मम ॥ 216 ॥
4.17.m:
What are the sixteen names of Rādhikā, O teacher of the world?
Tell them to me, your disciple; my curiosity to hear is great.

4.17.s:
śrutaṃ nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ ca sāmavede nirūpitam ..
tathā'pi śrotumicchāmi tvatto nāmāni ṣoḍaśa .. 217 ..
4.17.d:
श्रुतं नाम्नां सहस्रं च सामवेदे निरूपितम् ॥
तथाऽपि श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तो नामानि षोडश ॥ 217 ॥
4.17.m:
A thousand names described in the Sāmaveda have been heard [by me];
nevertheless, I wish to hear the sixteen names from you—

4.17.s:
abhyaṃtarāṇi teṣāṃ vā tadanyānyeva me vibho ..
aho puṇyasvarūpāṇi bhaktānāṃ vāñchitāni ca .. 218 ..
4.17.d:
अभ्यंतराणि तेषां वा तदन्यान्येव मे विभो ॥
अहो पुण्यस्वरूपाणि भक्तानां वाञ्छितानि च ॥ 218 ॥
4.17.m:
whether they are included among those, or quite different from them, O Lord!
Oh, they are the very essence of merit and desired by the devotees!

4.17.s:
nāmāni teṣāṃ vyutpattiṃ sarveṣāṃ durlabhāni ca ..
pāvanāni jaganmāturjagatāmapi kāraṇam .. 219 ..
4.17.d:
नामानि तेषां व्युत्पत्तिं सर्वेषां दुर्लभानि च ॥
पावनानि जगन्मातुर्जगतामपि कारणम् ॥ 219 ॥
4.17.m:
[Tell me] their names and their etymology, which are difficult to attain for all,
which purify, belonging to the Mother of the world, who is the cause of all worlds.

4.17.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
rādhā rāseśvarī rāsavāsinī rasikeśvarī ..
kṛṣṇaprāṇādhikā kṛṣṇapriyā kṛṣṇasvarūpiṇī .. 4.17.220 ..
4.17.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
राधा रासेश्वरी रासवासिनी रसिकेश्वरी ॥
कृष्णप्राणाधिका कृष्णप्रिया कृष्णस्वरूपिणी ॥ 4.17.220 ॥
4.17.m:
Rādhā, Rāseśvarī, Rāsavāsinī, Rasikeśvarī,
Kṛṣṇaprāṇādhikā, Kṛṣṇapriyā, Kṛṣṇasvarūpiṇī,

4.17.s:
kṛṣṇavāmāṃgasaṃbhūtā paramānandarūpiṇī ..
kṛṣṇā vṛndāvanī vṛndā vṛndāvanavinodinī .. 221 ..
4.17.d:
कृष्णवामांगसंभूता परमानन्दरूपिणी ॥
कृष्णा वृन्दावनी वृन्दा वृन्दावनविनोदिनी ॥ 221 ॥
4.17.m:
Kṛṣṇavāmāṅgasaṃbhūtā, Paramānandarūpiṇī,
Kṛṣṇā, Vṛndāvanī, Vṛndā, Vṛndāvanavinodinī,

4.17.s:
candrāvatī candrakāntā śatacandranibhānanā ..
nāmānyetāni sārāṇi teṣāmabhyantarāṇi ca .. 222 ..
4.17.d:
चन्द्रावती चन्द्रकान्ता शतचन्द्रनिभानना ॥
नामान्येतानि साराणि तेषामभ्यन्तराणि च ॥ 222 ॥
4.17.m:
Candrāvatī, Candrakāntā, Śatacandranibhānanā—
these are the essential names among them, and their inner [meanings]:

4.17.s:
rādhetyevaṃ ca saṃsiddhā rākāro dānavācakaḥ ..
svayaṃ nirvāṇadātrī yā sā rādhā parikīrtitā .. 223 ..
4.17.d:
राधेत्येवं च संसिद्धा राकारो दानवाचकः ॥
स्वयं निर्वाणदात्री या सा राधा परिकीर्तिता ॥ 223 ॥
4.17.m:
She is accomplished as 'Rādhā'; the syllable 'rā' signifies giving;
she who personally gives liberation (nirvāṇa) is proclaimed as Rādhā.

4.17.s:
rāseśvarasya patnīyaṃ tena rāseśvarī smṛtā ..
rāse ca vāso yasyāśca tena sā rāsavāsinī .. 224 ..
4.17.d:
रासेश्वरस्य पत्नीयं तेन रासेश्वरी स्मृता ॥
रासे च वासो यस्याश्च तेन सा रासवासिनी ॥ 224 ॥
4.17.m:
She is the wife of the Lord of the Rāsa dance; therefore she is remembered as Rāseśvarī.
And her dwelling is in the Rāsa dance; therefore she is Rāsavāsinī.

4.17.s:
sarvāsāṃ rasikānāṃ ca devīnāmīśvarī parā ..
pravadanti purā santastena tāṃ rasikeśvarīm .. 225 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वासां रसिकानां च देवीनामीश्वरी परा ॥
प्रवदन्ति पुरा सन्तस्तेन तां रसिकेश्वरीम् ॥ 225 ॥
4.17.m:
She is the supreme sovereign of all connoisseur goddesses;
therefore the virtuous ancient ones call her Rasikeśvarī.

4.17.s:
prāṇādhikā preyasī sā kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ ..
kṛṣṇaprāṇādhikā sā ca kṛṣṇena parikīrtitā ..226..
4.17.d:
प्राणाधिका प्रेयसी सा कृष्णस्य परमात्मनः ॥
कृष्णप्राणाधिका सा च कृष्णेन परिकीर्तिता ॥226॥
4.17.m:
She is the beloved dearer than life to Kṛṣṇa, the Paramātman;
and she is proclaimed by Kṛṣṇa as Kṛṣṇaprāṇādhikā.

4.17.s:
kṛṣṇasyātipriyā kāntā kṛṣṇo vā'syāḥ priyaḥ sadā ..
sarvairdevagaṇairuktā tena kṛṣṇapriyā smṛtā .. 227 ..
4.17.d:
कृष्णस्यातिप्रिया कान्ता कृष्णो वाऽस्याः प्रियः सदा ॥
सर्वैर्देवगणैरुक्ता तेन कृष्णप्रिया स्मृता ॥ 227 ॥
4.17.m:
She is the exceedingly beloved spouse of Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇa is ever her beloved;
declared thus by all the hosts of gods, she is remembered as Kṛṣṇapriyā.

4.17.s:
kṛṣṇarūpaṃ sannidhātuṃ yā śaktā cāvalīlayā ..
sarvāṃśaiḥ kṛṣṇasadṛśī tena kṛṣṇasvarūpiṇī .. 228 ..
4.17.d:
कृष्णरूपं सन्निधातुं या शक्ता चावलीलया ॥
सर्वांशैः कृष्णसदृशी तेन कृष्णस्वरूपिणी ॥ 228 ॥
4.17.m:
She who is able to assume the form of Kṛṣṇa with ease,
and is equal to Kṛṣṇa in all aspects, is therefore Kṛṣṇasvarūpiṇī.

4.17.s:
vāmāṅgārdhena kṛṣṇasya yā saṃbhūtā parā satī ..
kṛṣṇavāmāṅgasaṃbhūtā tena kṛṣṇena kīrtitā .. 229 ..
4.17.d:
वामाङ्गार्धेन कृष्णस्य या संभूता परा सती ॥
कृष्णवामाङ्गसंभूता तेन कृष्णेन कीर्तिता ॥ 229 ॥
4.17.m:
The supreme chaste woman who was born from the left half of Kṛṣṇa's body
is therefore proclaimed by Kṛṣṇa as Kṛṣṇavāmāṅgasaṃbhūtā.

4.17.s:
paramānandarāśiśca svayaṃ mūrtimatī satī ..
śrutibhiḥ kīrtitā tena paramānandarūpiṇī .. 4.17.230 ..
4.17.d:
परमानन्दराशिश्च स्वयं मूर्तिमती सती ॥
श्रुतिभिः कीर्तिता तेन परमानन्दरूपिणी ॥ 4.17.230 ॥
4.17.m:
The chaste woman who is herself the mass of supreme bliss incarnate
is therefore proclaimed by the Vedas as Paramānandarūpiṇī.

4.17.s:
kṛṣirmokṣārthavacano na evotkṛṣṭavācakaḥ ..
ākāro dātṛvacanastena kṛṣṇā prakīrtitā ..231..
4.17.d:
कृषिर्मोक्षार्थवचनो न एवोत्कृष्टवाचकः ॥
आकारो दातृवचनस्तेन कृष्णा प्रकीर्तिता ॥231॥
4.17.m:
The root 'kṛṣ' signifies liberation; 'ṇa' signifies excellence;
the syllable 'ā' signifies the giver; therefore she is celebrated as Kṛṣṇā.

4.17.s:
asti vṛndāvanaṃ yasyāstena vṛndāvanī smṛtā ..
vṛndāvanasyādhidevī tena vā'tha prakīrtitā ..232..
4.17.d:
अस्ति वृन्दावनं यस्यास्तेन वृन्दावनी स्मृता ॥
वृन्दावनस्याधिदेवी तेन वाऽथ प्रकीर्तिता ॥232॥
4.17.m:
Vṛndāvana belongs to her, therefore she is remembered as Vṛndāvanī;
or else she is celebrated because she is the presiding deity of Vṛndāvana.

4.17.s:
saṃghaḥ sakhīnāṃ vṛndaḥ syādakāro'pyastivācakaḥ ..
sakhivṛndo'sti yasyāśca sā vṛndā parikīrtitā ..233..
4.17.d:
संघः सखीनां वृन्दः स्यादकारोऽप्यस्तिवाचकः ॥
सखिवृन्दोऽस्ति यस्याश्च सा वृन्दा परिकीर्तिता ॥233॥
4.17.m:
'Vṛnda' means a group of female companions, and 'a' signifies existence;
and she who has a group of female companions is proclaimed as Vṛndā.

4.17.s:
vṛndāvane vinodaśca so'syā hyasti ca tatra vai ..
vedā vadanti tāṃ tena vṛndāvanavinodinīm..234..
4.17.d:
वृन्दावने विनोदश्च सोऽस्या ह्यस्ति च तत्र वै ॥
वेदा वदन्ति तां तेन वृन्दावनविनोदिनीम्॥234॥
4.17.m:
She indeed has her delight in Vṛndāvana, there indeed;
therefore the Vedas call her Vṛndāvanavinodinī.

4.17.s:
nakhacandrāvalīvakracandro'sti yatra saṃtatam..
tena candrāvalī sā ca kṛṣṇena parikīrtitā ..235..
4.17.d:
नखचन्द्रावलीवक्रचन्द्रोऽस्ति यत्र संततम्॥
तेन चन्द्रावली सा च कृष्णेन परिकीर्तिता ॥235॥
4.17.m:
Where the curved moon of the rows of moon-like nails constantly exists,
therefore she is proclaimed as Candrāvalī by Kṛṣṇa.

4.17.s:
candratulyā kāntirasti sadā yasyā divāniśam ..
sā candrakāntā harṣeṇa hariṇā parikīrtitā .. 236 ..
4.17.d:
चन्द्रतुल्या कान्तिरस्ति सदा यस्या दिवानिशम् ॥
सा चन्द्रकान्ता हर्षेण हरिणा परिकीर्तिता ॥ 236 ॥
4.17.m:
She whose radiance is equal to the moon always, day and night,
is proclaimed with joy as Candrakāntā by Hari.

4.17.s:
śaraccandraprabhā yasyāścānane'sti divāniśam ..
muninā kīrtitā tena śaraccandraprabhānanā .. 237 ..
4.17.d:
शरच्चन्द्रप्रभा यस्याश्चाननेऽस्ति दिवानिशम् ॥
मुनिना कीर्तिता तेन शरच्चन्द्रप्रभानना ॥ 237 ॥
4.17.m:
She whose face possesses the splendour of the autumn moon day and night
is therefore celebrated by the sage as Śaraccandraprabhānanā.

4.17.s:
idaṃ ṣoḍaśanāmoktamarthavyākhyānasaṃyutam ..
nārāyaṇena yaddattaṃ brahmaṇe nābhipaṅkaje ..238..
4.17.d:
इदं षोडशनामोक्तमर्थव्याख्यानसंयुतम् ॥
नारायणेन यद्दत्तं ब्रह्मणे नाभिपङ्कजे ॥238॥
4.17.m: This hymn of sixteen names, endowed with the explanation of their meanings,

4.17.s:
brahmaṇā ca purā dattaṃ dharmāya janakāya me ..
dharmeṇa kṛpayā dattaṃ mahyamādityaparvaṇi .. 239 ..
4.17.d:
ब्रह्मणा च पुरा दत्तं धर्माय जनकाय मे ॥
धर्मेण कृपया दत्तं मह्यमादित्यपर्वणि ॥ 239 ॥
4.17.m:
And in ancient times it was given by Brahmā to Dharma, my father;
and out of compassion it was given by Dharma to me on the solar festival,

4.17.s:
puṣkare ca mahātīrthe puṇyāhe devasaṃsadi ..
rādhāprabhāvaprastāve suprasannena cetasā .. 4.17.240 ..
4.17.d:
पुष्करे च महातीर्थे पुण्याहे देवसंसदि ॥
राधाप्रभावप्रस्तावे सुप्रसन्नेन चेतसा ॥ 4.17.240 ॥
4.17.m:
at the great holy site of Puṣkara, on an auspicious day, in an assembly of the gods,
during the discourse on Rādhā's greatness, with a well-pleased mind.

4.17.s:
idaṃ stotraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ tubhyaṃ dattaṃ mayā mune ..
nindakāyāvaiṣṇavāya na dātavyaṃ mahāmune .. 241 ..
4.17.d:
इदं स्तोत्रं महापुण्यं तुभ्यं दत्तं मया मुने ॥
निन्दकायावैष्णवाय न दातव्यं महामुने ॥ 241 ॥
4.17.m:
This greatly meritorious hymn has been given by me to you, O sage;
it must not be given to a censurer or to a non-Vaiṣṇava, O great sage.

4.17.s:
yāvajjīvamidaṃ stotraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ ..
rādhāmādhavayoḥ pādapadme bhaktirbhavediha .. 242 ..
4.17.d:
यावज्जीवमिदं स्तोत्रं त्रिसंध्यं यः पठेन्नरः ॥
राधामाधवयोः पादपद्मे भक्तिर्भवेदिह ॥ 242 ॥
4.17.m:
Whatever person recites this hymn lifelong at the three junctures of the day,
devotion to the lotus feet of Rādhā and Mādhava arises in this world.

4.17.s:
ante labhettayordāsyaṃ śaśvatsahacaro bhavet ..
aṇimādikasiddhiṃ ca saṃprāpya nityavigraham .. 243 ..
4.17.d:
अन्ते लभेत्तयोर्दास्यं शश्वत्सहचरो भवेत् ॥
अणिमादिकसिद्धिं च संप्राप्य नित्यविग्रहम् ॥ 243 ॥
4.17.m:
In the end he attains servitude to them both and becomes their eternal companion,
and having attained the supernormal power beginning with anima and an eternal body.

4.17.s:
vratadānopavāsaiśca sarvairniyamapūrvakaiḥ ..
caturṇāṃ caiva vedānāṃ pāṭhaiḥ sarvārthasaṃyutaiḥ .. 244 ..
4.17.d:
व्रतदानोपवासैश्च सर्वैर्नियमपूर्वकैः ॥
चतुर्णां चैव वेदानां पाठैः सर्वार्थसंयुतैः ॥ 244 ॥
4.17.m:
Whatever fruit is gained through vows, gifts, and fasts preceded by all regulations,
and through recitations of the four Vedas accompanied by all their meanings,

4.17.s:
sarveṣāṃ yajñatīrthānāṃ karaṇairvidhibodhitaiḥ ..
pradakṣiṇena bhūmeśca kṛtsnāyā eva saptadhā .. 245 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वेषां यज्ञतीर्थानां करणैर्विधिबोधितैः ॥
प्रदक्षिणेन भूमेश्च कृत्स्नाया एव सप्तधा ॥ 245 ॥
4.17.m:
through the performance of all sacrifices and pilgrimages according to injunction,
through circumambulating the entire earth seven times,

4.17.s:
śaraṇāgatarakṣāyāmajñānāṃ jñānadānataḥ ..
devānāṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca darśanenāpi yatphalam .. 246 ..
4.17.d:
शरणागतरक्षायामज्ञानां ज्ञानदानतः ॥
देवानां वैष्णवानां च दर्शनेनापि यत्फलम् ॥ 246 ॥
4.17.m:
in protecting those who take refuge, through imparting knowledge to the ignorant,
and even through the vision of gods and Vaiṣṇavas—

4.17.s:
tadeva stotrapāṭhasya kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm ..
stotrasyāsya prabhāveṇa jīvanmukto bhavennaraḥ .. 247 ..
4.17.d:
तदेव स्तोत्रपाठस्य कलां नार्हति षोडशीम् ॥
स्तोत्रस्यास्य प्रभावेण जीवन्मुक्तो भवेन्नरः ॥ 247 ॥
4.17.m:
that does not equal one sixteenth part of the recitation of this hymn.
By the power of this hymn, a man becomes liberated while living.

4.17.s:
nārada uvāca ..
saṃprāptaṃ paramāścaryaṃ stotraṃ sarvasudurlabham ..
kavacaṃ cāpi devyāśca saṃsāravijayaṃ prabho .. .. 248 ..
4.17.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
संप्राप्तं परमाश्चर्यं स्तोत्रं सर्वसुदुर्लभम् ॥
कवचं चापि देव्याश्च संसारविजयं प्रभो ॥ ॥ 248 ॥
4.17.m:
The most wonderful hymn of praise, exceedingly hard to obtain for anyone, has been received,
and also the goddess's armour that conquers worldly existence, O Lord.

4.17.s:
kṛtaṃ stotraṃ suyatnena prāptaṃ tadapi durlabham ..
śrutvā kṛṣṇakathāṃ citrāṃ tvatpādābjaprasādataḥ .. 249 ..
4.17.d:
कृतं स्तोत्रं सुयत्नेन प्राप्तं तदपि दुर्लभम् ॥
श्रुत्वा कृष्णकथां चित्रां त्वत्पादाब्जप्रसादतः ॥ 249 ॥
4.17.m:
With great effort the hymn of praise was composed, and that which is difficult to attain has also been obtained,
having heard the wondrous story of Kṛṣṇa by the grace of your lotus feet.

4.17.s:
adhunā śrotumicchāmi yadrahasyaṃ ca tadvada ..
prātaśca nagaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kimūcurballavā mune .. 4.17.250 ..
4.17.d:
अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि यद्रहस्यं च तद्वद ॥
प्रातश्च नगरं दृष्ट्वा किमूचुर्बल्लवा मुने ॥ 4.17.250 ॥
4.17.m:
Now I wish to hear whatever is secret; tell me that.
In the morning, upon seeing the city, what did the cowherds say, O sage?

4.17.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
gatāyāṃ tatra yāminyāṃ gate ca viśvakarmaṇi ..
aruṇodayavelāyāṃ janāḥ sarve jajāgaruḥ .. 251 ..
4.17.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
गतायां तत्र यामिन्यां गते च विश्वकर्मणि ॥
अरुणोदयवेलायां जनाः सर्वे जजागरुः ॥ 251 ॥
4.17.m:
When the night had passed and Viśvakarman had departed,
at dawn all the people awoke.

4.17.s:
utthāya dṛṣṭvā nagaraṃ sarvebhyo'pi vilakṣaṇam ..
kimāścaryaṃ kimāścaryamityūcurvrajavāsinaḥ .. 252 ..
4.17.d:
उत्थाय दृष्ट्वा नगरं सर्वेभ्योऽपि विलक्षणम् ॥
किमाश्चर्यं किमाश्चर्यमित्यूचुर्व्रजवासिनः ॥ 252 ॥
4.17.m:
Arising and seeing the city, distinctive above all others,
"What a wonder! What a wonder!" the inhabitants of Vraja exclaimed.

4.17.s:
kāścidgopānkecidūcuḥ kuta etadabhūdidam ..
na jāne kena rūpeṇa ko bhūmau prabhavediti .. 253 ..
4.17.d:
काश्चिद्गोपान्केचिदूचुः कुत एतदभूदिदम् ॥
न जाने केन रूपेण को भूमौ प्रभवेदिति ॥ 253 ॥
4.17.m:
Some spoke to certain cowherds: "From where did this come about?
I do not know who, in what form, could accomplish this on earth."

4.17.s:
bubudhe manasā nando gargavākyamanusmaran ..
śrīharericchayā sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram .. 254 ..
4.17.d:
बुबुधे मनसा नन्दो गर्गवाक्यमनुस्मरन् ॥
श्रीहरेरिच्छया सर्वं जगदेतच्चराचरम् ॥ 254 ॥
4.17.m:
Recalling the words of Garga, Nanda understood in his mind:
"All this moving and unmoving world exists by the will of Śrī Hari.

4.17.s:
brahmāditṛṇaparyantaṃ yasya bhrūbhaṅgalīlayā ..
āvirbhūtaṃ tirobhūtaṃ tasyāsādhyaṃ ca kiṃ kutaḥ .. 255 ..
4.17.d:
ब्रह्मादितृणपर्यन्तं यस्य भ्रूभङ्गलीलया ॥
आविर्भूतं तिरोभूतं तस्यासाध्यं च किं कुतः ॥ 255 ॥
4.17.m:
For Him, by whose playful knitting of the brows from Brahmā down to a blade of grass
everything appears and disappears—what could be impossible for Him, and whence?

4.17.s:
vivareṣveva yallomnāṃ brahmāṇḍānyakhilāni ca ..
īśasya tanmahāviṣṇoḥ kimasādhyaṃ hareraho .. 256 ..
4.17.d:
विवरेष्वेव यल्लोम्नां ब्रह्माण्डान्यखिलानि च ॥
ईशस्य तन्महाविष्णोः किमसाध्यं हरेरहो ॥ 256 ॥
4.17.m:
In the pores of whose body-hair all the cosmic eggs reside,
for that Lord Mahāviṣṇu, for Hari—ah, what is impossible?

4.17.s:
brahmānanteśadharmāśca dhyāyante yatpadāmbujam ..
kimasādhyaṃ tadīśasya māyāmānuṣarūpiṇaḥ .. 257 ..
4.17.d:
ब्रह्मानन्तेशधर्माश्च ध्यायन्ते यत्पदाम्बुजम् ॥
किमसाध्यं तदीशस्य मायामानुषरूपिणः ॥ 257 ॥
4.17.m:
Brahmā, Ananta, the Lord [Śiva], and Dharma meditate upon His lotus feet;
what is impossible for that Lord who has taken the form of an illusory human?"

4.17.s:
bhrāmaṃbhrāmaṃ tannagaraṃ darśaṃdarśaṃ gṛhaṃgṛham ..
pāṭhaṃpāṭhaṃ ca nāmāni sarvebhyo nilayaṃ dadau .. 258 ..
4.17.d:
भ्रामंभ्रामं तन्नगरं दर्शंदर्शं गृहंगृहम् ॥
पाठंपाठं च नामानि सर्वेभ्यो निलयं ददौ ॥ 258 ॥
4.17.m:
Wandering around that city again and again, looking at house after house,
and reading name after name, he assigned a residence to everyone.

4.17.s:
kṛtvā śubhakṣaṇaṃ nando vṛṣabhānaśca kautukī ..
cakāra sagaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ mudā''śramaniveśanam .. 259 ..
4.17.d:
कृत्वा शुभक्षणं नन्दो वृषभानश्च कौतुकी ॥
चकार सगणैः सार्द्धं मुदा'ऽश्रमनिवेशनम् ॥ 259 ॥
4.17.m:
Having chosen an auspicious moment, Nanda and the delighted Vṛṣabhānu,
together with their retinues, joyfully entered their dwellings.

4.17.s:
sarve vṛndāvanasthāśca prasannavadanekṣaṇāḥ ..
mudā praveśanaṃ cakruḥ svasvamāśramamuttamam .. 4.17.260 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वे वृन्दावनस्थाश्च प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणाः ॥
मुदा प्रवेशनं चक्रुः स्वस्वमाश्रममुत्तमम् ॥ 4.17.260 ॥
4.17.m:
And all those dwelling in Vṛndāvana, their faces and eyes cheerful,
joyfully entered their respective excellent abodes.

4.17.s:
sarve mumudire gopāḥ svesve sthāne manohare ..
bālakā bālikāścaiva cikrīḍuśca praharṣitāḥ .. 261 ..
4.17.d:
सर्वे मुमुदिरे गोपाः स्वेस्वे स्थाने मनोहरे ॥
बालका बालिकाश्चैव चिक्रीडुश्च प्रहर्षिताः ॥ 261 ॥
4.17.m:
All the cowherds rejoiced in their own charming places,
and the boys and girls, overjoyed, played together.

4.17.s:
śrīkṛṣṇo baladevaśca śiśubhiḥ saha kautukāt ..
krīḍāṃ cakāra tatraiva sthānesthāne manohare .. 262 ..
4.17.d:
श्रीकृष्णो बलदेवश्च शिशुभिः सह कौतुकात् ॥
क्रीडां चकार तत्रैव स्थानेस्थाने मनोहरे ॥ 262 ॥
4.17.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Baladeva, in high spirits, along with the children,
sported right there, in various charming places.

4.17.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ nirmāṇaṃ nagarasya ca ..
abalānāṃ vane rāsamaṇḍalasya ca nārada .. 263 ..
4.17.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं निर्माणं नगरस्य च ॥
अबलानां वने रासमण्डलस्य च नारद ॥ 263 ॥
4.17.m:
Thus all the construction of the city has been told,
as well as that of the rāsa-circle of the women in the forest, O Nārada.

4.18.s:
.. śaunaka uvāca ..
aho kimadbhutaṃ sūta rahasyaṃ sumanoharam ..
śrutaṃ kṛṣṇasya caritaṃ sukhadaṃ mokṣadaṃ param .. 1 ..
4.18.d:
॥ शौनक उवाच ॥
अहो किमद्भुतं सूत रहस्यं सुमनोहरम् ॥
श्रुतं कृष्णस्य चरितं सुखदं मोक्षदं परम् ॥ 1 ॥

4.18.s:
sūta uvāca ..
śrutvā nagaranirmāṇaṃ nārado munisattamaḥ ..
papraccha kṛṣṇacaritamaparaṃ sumanoharam .. 2 ..
4.18.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
श्रुत्वा नगरनिर्माणं नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ॥
पप्रच्छ कृष्णचरितमपरं सुमनोहरम् ॥ 2 ॥

4.18.s:
nārada uvāca ..
śrīkṛṣṇākhyānacaritaṃ pīyūṣamṛṣisattama ..
jñānasiṃdho nigada māṃ śiṣyaṃ ca śaraṇāgatam .. 3 ..
4.18.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
श्रीकृष्णाख्यानचरितं पीयूषमृषिसत्तम ॥
ज्ञानसिंधो निगद मां शिष्यं च शरणागतम् ॥ 3 ॥

4.18.s:
nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā mudā nārāyaṇaḥ svayam ..
uvāca paramīśasya caritaṃ paramādbhutam .. 4 ..
4.18.d:
नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मुदा नारायणः स्वयम् ॥
उवाच परमीशस्य चरितं परमाद्भुतम् ॥ 4 ॥

4.18.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ekadā bālakaiḥ sārdhaṃ balena saha mādhavaḥ ..
jagāma śrīmadhuvanaṃ yamunātīranīrajam .. 5 ..
4.18.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
एकदा बालकैः सार्धं बलेन सह माधवः ॥
जगाम श्रीमधुवनं यमुनातीरनीरजम् ॥ 5 ॥

4.18.s:
vicerurgosahasraiśca cikrīḍurbālakāstadā ..
viśrāntāstṛṭparītāśca kṣudhā ca paripīḍitāḥ .. 6 ..
4.18.d:
विचेरुर्गोसहस्रैश्च चिक्रीडुर्बालकास्तदा ॥
विश्रान्तास्तृट्परीताश्च क्षुधा च परिपीडिताः ॥ 6 ॥

4.18.s:
tamūcurgopaśiśavaḥ śrīkṛṣṇaṃ parayā mudā ..
kṣudasmānbādhate kṛṣṇa kiṃ kurmo brūhi kiṃkarān..7..
4.18.d:
तमूचुर्गोपशिशवः श्रीकृष्णं परया मुदा ॥
क्षुदस्मान्बाधते कृष्ण किं कुर्मो ब्रूहि किंकरान्॥7॥

4.18.s:
śiśūnāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā tānuvāca dayānidhiḥ ..
hitaṃ tathyaṃ ca vacanaṃ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ ..8..
4.18.d:
शिशूनां वचनं श्रुत्वा तानुवाच दयानिधिः ॥
हितं तथ्यं च वचनं प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ॥8॥

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
bālā gacchata viprāṇāṃ yajñasthānaṃ sukhāvaham ..
annaṃ yācata tāñchīghraṃ brāhmaṇāṃśca kratūnmukhān .. 9 ..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
बाला गच्छत विप्राणां यज्ञस्थानं सुखावहम् ॥
अन्नं याचत ताञ्छीघ्रं ब्राह्मणांश्च क्रतून्मुखान् ॥ 9 ॥

4.18.s:
viprā āṃgirasāḥ sarve svāśrame śrīvanāntike ..
yajñaṃ kurvanti viprāśca śrutismṛtiviśāradāḥ ..4.18.10..
4.18.d:
विप्रा आंगिरसाः सर्वे स्वाश्रमे श्रीवनान्तिके ॥
यज्ञं कुर्वन्ति विप्राश्च श्रुतिस्मृतिविशारदाः ॥4.18.10॥

4.18.s:
niḥspṛhā vaiṣṇavāḥ sarve māṃ yajanti mumukṣavaḥ.
māyayā māṃ na jānanti māyāmānuṣarūpiṇam .. 11 ..
4.18.d:
निःस्पृहा वैष्णवाः सर्वे मां यजन्ति मुमुक्षवः।
मायया मां न जानन्ति मायामानुषरूपिणम् ॥ 11 ॥

4.18.s:
na ceddadati yuṣmabhyamannaṃ viprāḥ kratūnmukhāḥ ..
tatkāntā yācata kṣipraṃ dayāyuktāḥ śiśūnprati .. 12 ..
4.18.d:
न चेद्ददति युष्मभ्यमन्नं विप्राः क्रतून्मुखाः ॥
तत्कान्ता याचत क्षिप्रं दयायुक्ताः शिशून्प्रति ॥ 12 ॥

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇavacanaṃ śrutvā yayurbālakapuṃgavāḥ ..
purato brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tasthurānamrakaṃdharāḥ .. 13 ..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्णवचनं श्रुत्वा ययुर्बालकपुंगवाः ॥
पुरतो ब्राह्मणानां च तस्थुरानम्रकंधराः ॥ 13 ॥

4.18.s:
ityūcurbālakāḥ śīghramannaṃ datta dvijottamāḥ ..
na śuśruvurdvijāḥ kecitkecicchrutvā sthitāḥ sthitāḥ..14..
4.18.d:
इत्यूचुर्बालकाः शीघ्रमन्नं दत्त द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
न शुश्रुवुर्द्विजाः केचित्केचिच्छ्रुत्वा स्थिताः स्थिताः॥14॥

4.18.s:
te yayū randhanāgāraṃ brāhmaṇyo yatra pācikāḥ ..
gatvā bālā viprabhāryāḥ praṇemurnatakandharāḥ .. 19 ..
4.18.d:
ते ययू रन्धनागारं ब्राह्मण्यो यत्र पाचिकाः ॥
गत्वा बाला विप्रभार्याः प्रणेमुर्नतकन्धराः ॥ 19 ॥

4.18.s:
natvocurbālakāḥ sarve viprabhāryāḥ pativratāḥ ..
annaṃ datta mātaro'smānkṣudhārtānbālakānapi .. 16 ..
4.18.d:
नत्वोचुर्बालकाः सर्वे विप्रभार्याः पतिव्रताः ॥
अन्नं दत्त मातरोऽस्मान्क्षुधार्तान्बालकानपि ॥ 16 ॥

4.18.s:
bālānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā tāṃśca manoharān ..
papracchuḥ sādaraṃ sādhvyaḥ smerānanasaroruhāḥ ..17..
4.18.d:
बालानां वचनं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा तांश्च मनोहरान् ॥
पप्रच्छुः सादरं साध्व्यः स्मेराननसरोरुहाः ॥17॥

4.18.s:
viprapatnya ūcuḥ ..
ke yūyaṃ preṣitāḥ kena kāni nāmāni kovidāḥ ..
dāsyāmo'nnaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vyañjanaiḥ sahitaṃ varam .. 18 ..
4.18.d:
विप्रपत्न्य ऊचुः ॥
के यूयं प्रेषिताः केन कानि नामानि कोविदाः ॥
दास्यामोऽन्नं बहुविधं व्यञ्जनैः सहितं वरम् ॥ 18 ॥

4.18.s:
brāhmaṇīnāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā tā ūcuste mudā'nvitāḥ ..
snigdhā hasantaḥ sphītāśca sarve gopālabālakāḥ .. 19 ..
4.18.d:
ब्राह्मणीनां वचः श्रुत्वा ता ऊचुस्ते मुदाऽन्विताः ॥
स्निग्धा हसन्तः स्फीताश्च सर्वे गोपालबालकाः ॥ 19 ॥

4.18.s:
bālā ūcuḥ ..
preṣitā rāmakṛṣṇābhyāṃ vayaṃ kṣutpīḍitā bhṛśam ..
dattānnaṃ mātaro'smabhyaṃ kṣipraṃ yāmastadantikam .. 4.18.20 ..
4.18.d:
बाला ऊचुः ॥
प्रेषिता रामकृष्णाभ्यां वयं क्षुत्पीडिता भृशम् ॥
दत्तान्नं मातरोऽस्मभ्यं क्षिप्रं यामस्तदन्तिकम् ॥ 4.18.20 ॥

4.18.s:
ito vidūre bhāṇḍīre vanābhyantarameva ca ..
vaṭamūle madhuvane vasantau rāmakeśavau .. 21 ..
4.18.d:
इतो विदूरे भाण्डीरे वनाभ्यन्तरमेव च ॥
वटमूले मधुवने वसन्तौ रामकेशवौ ॥ 21 ॥

4.18.s:
viśrāntau kṣudhitau tau ca yācete'nnaṃ ca mātaraḥ ..
kimu deyamadeyaṃ vā śīghraṃ vadata no'dhunā .. 22 ..
4.18.d:
विश्रान्तौ क्षुधितौ तौ च याचेतेऽन्नं च मातरः ॥
किमु देयमदेयं वा शीघ्रं वदत नोऽधुना ॥ 22 ॥

4.18.s:
gopānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭānandāśrulocanāḥ ..
pulakāṃkitasarvāṃgāstatpādābjamanorathāḥ .. 23 ..
4.18.d:
गोपानां वचनं श्रुत्वा हृष्टानन्दाश्रुलोचनाः ॥
पुलकांकितसर्वांगास्तत्पादाब्जमनोरथाः ॥ 23 ॥

4.18.s:
nānāvyañjanasaṃyuktaṃ śālyannaṃ sumanoharam..
pāyasaṃ piṣṭakaṃ svādu dadhi kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu .. 24 ..
4.18.d:
नानाव्यञ्जनसंयुक्तं शाल्यन्नं सुमनोहरम्॥
पायसं पिष्टकं स्वादु दधि क्षीरं घृतं मधु ॥ 24 ॥

4.18.s:
raupye kāṃsye rājate ca pātre kṛtvā mudā'nvitāḥ ..
tāḥ sarvā viprapatnyaśca prayayuḥ kṛṣṇasannidhim .. 25 ..
4.18.d:
रौप्ये कांस्ये राजते च पात्रे कृत्वा मुदाऽन्विताः ॥
ताः सर्वा विप्रपत्न्यश्च प्रययुः कृष्णसन्निधिम् ॥ 25 ॥
4.18.m:
and placing them in vessels of silver, bronze, and brass, filled with joy,
all those wives of the Brahmins set forth into Kṛṣṇa's presence.

4.18.s:
nānāmanorathaṃ kṛtvā manasā gamanotsukāḥ ..
pativratāstā dhanyāśca śrīkṛṣṇadarśanotsukāḥ .. 26 ..
4.18.d:
नानामनोरथं कृत्वा मनसा गमनोत्सुकाः ॥
पतिव्रतास्ता धन्याश्च श्रीकृष्णदर्शनोत्सुकाः ॥ 26 ॥
4.18.m:
Conceiving various desires, eager in mind to depart,
those blessed, devoted wives were eager to see Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇaṃ dadṛśurgatvā rāmaṃ ca saha bālakam ..
vaṭamūle vasantaṃ tamuḍumadhye yathoḍupam .. 27 ..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्णं ददृशुर्गत्वा रामं च सह बालकम् ॥
वटमूले वसन्तं तमुडुमध्ये यथोडुपम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.18.m:
Having gone, they saw Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and Rāma together with the [other] boys,
abiding at the foot of the banyan tree like the moon in the midst of stars:

4.18.s:
śyāmaṃ kiśoravayasaṃ pītakauśeyavāsasam ..
sundaraṃ sasmitaṃ śāntaṃ rādhākāntaṃ manoharam ..28..
4.18.d:
श्यामं किशोरवयसं पीतकौशेयवाससम् ॥
सुन्दरं सस्मितं शान्तं राधाकान्तं मनोहरम् ॥28॥
4.18.m:
dark-complexioned, youthful in age, dressed in yellow silk garments,
handsome, smiling, tranquil, the beloved of Rādhā, captivating,

4.18.s:
śaratpārvaṇacandrāsyaṃ ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitam ..
ratnakuṇḍalayugmābhyāṃ gaṇḍasthalavirājitam .. 29 ..
4.18.d:
शरत्पार्वणचन्द्रास्यं रत्नालंकारभूषितम् ॥
रत्नकुण्डलयुग्माभ्यां गण्डस्थलविराजितम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.18.m:
his face like the full moon of autumn, adorned with jewel ornaments,
his cheeks shining with a pair of jewelled earrings,

4.18.s:
ratnakeyūravalayaratnanūpurabhūṣitam ..
ājānulambitāṃ śubhrāṃ bibhrataṃ ratnamālikām .. 4.18.30 ..
4.18.d:
रत्नकेयूरवलयरत्ननूपुरभूषितम् ॥
आजानुलम्बितां शुभ्रां बिभ्रतं रत्नमालिकाम् ॥ 4.18.30 ॥
4.18.m: wearing a bright necklace of jewels hanging down to his knees,

4.18.s:
mālatīmālayā kaṇṭhavakṣaḥsthalavirājitam..
candanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumāñcitavigraham ..31 ..
4.18.d:
मालतीमालया कण्ठवक्षःस्थलविराजितम्॥
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीकुङ्कुमाञ्चितविग्रहम् ॥31 ॥
4.18.m:
his neck and chest resplendent with a garland of mālatī flowers,
his body smeared with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron,

4.18.s:
sunakhaṃ sukapolaṃ ca pakva bimbādharaṃ varam ..
pakvadāḍimabījābhaṃ bibhrataṃ dantamuttamam .. 32 ..
4.18.d:
सुनखं सुकपोलं च पक्व बिम्बाधरं वरम् ॥
पक्वदाडिमबीजाभं बिभ्रतं दन्तमुत्तमम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.18.m:
having beautiful nails, lovely cheeks, and excellent lips red like ripe bimba fruit,
bearing excellent teeth resembling the seeds of a ripe pomegranate,

4.18.s:
śikhipicchasamāyuktaṃ baddhacūḍaṃ parātparam..
kadambapuṣpayugmābhyāṃ karṇamūle virājitam .. 33 ..
4.18.d:
शिखिपिच्छसमायुक्तं बद्धचूडं परात्परम्॥
कदम्बपुष्पयुग्माभ्यां कर्णमूले विराजितम् ॥ 33 ॥
4.18.m:
adorned with a peacock feather, his topknot bound, the highest of the high,
resplendent with a pair of kadamba flowers at the base of his ears,

4.18.s:
dhyānāsādhyaṃ yogināṃ ca bhaktānugrahakātaram..
brahmeśadharmaśeṣendraiḥ stūyamānaṃ munīśvaraiḥ .. 34 ..
4.18.d:
ध्यानासाध्यं योगिनां च भक्तानुग्रहकातरम्॥
ब्रह्मेशधर्मशेषेन्द्रैः स्तूयमानं मुनीश्वरैः ॥ 34 ॥
4.18.m:
unattainable by meditation even for yogins, yet moved by grace toward his devotees,
praised by Brahmā, Īśa, Dharma, Śeṣa, Indra, and the lords among sages.

4.18.s:
dṛṣṭvaivamīśvaraṃ bhaktyā praṇemurdvijayoṣitaḥ ..
svānāṃ jñānānurūpaṃ ca tuṣṭuvurmadhusūdanam .. 35 ..
4.18.d:
दृष्ट्वैवमीश्वरं भक्त्या प्रणेमुर्द्विजयोषितः ॥
स्वानां ज्ञानानुरूपं च तुष्टुवुर्मधुसूदनम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.18.m:
Seeing the Lord thus, the wives of the twice-born bowed with devotion,
and according to their own knowledge, they praised Madhusūdana.

4.18.s:
viprapatnya ūcuḥ ..
tvaṃ brahma paramaṃ dhāma nirīho nirahaṃkṛtiḥ ..
nirguṇaśca nirākāraḥ sākāraḥ saguṇaḥ svayam ..36..
4.18.d:
विप्रपत्न्य ऊचुः ॥
त्वं ब्रह्म परमं धाम निरीहो निरहंकृतिः ॥
निर्गुणश्च निराकारः साकारः सगुणः स्वयम् ॥36॥
4.18.m:
"You are Brahman, the supreme abode, devoid of longing, free from egoism,
without gunas and formless, yet yourself endowed with form and with gunas,

4.18.s:
sākṣirūpaśca nirliptaḥ paramātmā nirākṛtiḥ ..
prakṛtiḥ puruṣastvaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca tayoḥ param.. 37..
4.18.d:
साक्षिरूपश्च निर्लिप्तः परमात्मा निराकृतिः ॥
प्रकृतिः पुरुषस्त्वं च कारणं च तयोः परम्॥ 37॥
4.18.m:
in the form of the witness, unattached, the Paramātman, formless.
You are Prakṛti and Puruṣa, and the supreme cause of both.

4.18.s:
sṛṣṭisthityantaviṣaye ye ca devāstrayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
te tvadaṃśāḥ sarvabījā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ .. .. 38 ..
4.18.d:
सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तविषये ये च देवास्त्रयः स्मृताः ॥
ते त्वदंशाः सर्वबीजा ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥ ॥ 38 ॥
4.18.m:
And the three gods who are mentioned regarding creation, maintenance, and destruction—
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, the seeds of all—are portions of you.

4.18.s:
yasya lomnāṃ ca vivare cākhilaṃ viśvamīśvara..
mahāvirāṇmahāviṣṇustvaṃ tasya janako vibho .. 39 ..
4.18.d:
यस्य लोम्नां च विवरे चाखिलं विश्वमीश्वर॥
महाविराण्महाविष्णुस्त्वं तस्य जनको विभो ॥ 39 ॥
4.18.m:
He in the pores of whose hair the entire universe rests, O Lord,
Mahāvirāj, Mahāviṣṇu—you are his progenitor, O all-pervading one!

4.18.s:
tejastvaṃ cāpi tejasvī jñānaṃ jñānī ca tatparaḥ ..
vede'nirvacanīyastvaṃ kastvāṃ stotumiheśvaraḥ .. 4.18.40 ..
4.18.d:
तेजस्त्वं चापि तेजस्वी ज्ञानं ज्ञानी च तत्परः ॥
वेदेऽनिर्वचनीयस्त्वं कस्त्वां स्तोतुमिहेश्वरः ॥ 4.18.40 ॥
4.18.m:
You are splendor, and also the splendid one; you are knowledge, the knower, and beyond that."
You are indescribable in the Veda; who is capable of praising you in this world, O Lord?

4.18.s:
mahadādisṛṣṭisūtraṃ pañcatanmātrameva ca ..
bījaṃ tvaṃ sarvaśaktīnāṃ sarvaśaktisvarūpakaḥ .. 41 ..
4.18.d:
महदादिसृष्टिसूत्रं पञ्चतन्मात्रमेव च ॥
बीजं त्वं सर्वशक्तीनां सर्वशक्तिस्वरूपकः ॥ 41 ॥
4.18.m:
You are the thread of creation beginning with Mahat, and the five subtle elements themselves;
You are the seed of all powers, your very nature is all powers.

4.18.s:
sarvaśaktīśvaraḥ sarvaḥ sarvaśaktyāśrayaḥ sadā ..
tvamanīhaḥ svayaṃjyotiḥ sarvānandaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 42 ..
4.18.d:
सर्वशक्तीश्वरः सर्वः सर्वशक्त्याश्रयः सदा ॥
त्वमनीहः स्वयंज्योतिः सर्वानन्दः सनातनः ॥ 42 ॥
4.18.m:
You are the lord of all powers, the All, and the eternal abode of all powers.
You are desireless, self-luminous, all-bliss, and eternal.

4.18.s:
aho'pyākārahīnastvaṃ sarvavigrahavānapi..
sarveṃdriyāṇāṃ viṣayaṃ jānāsi nendriyī bhavān .. 43 ..
4.18.d:
अहोऽप्याकारहीनस्त्वं सर्वविग्रहवानपि॥
सर्वेंद्रियाणां विषयं जानासि नेन्द्रियी भवान् ॥ 43 ॥
4.18.m:
Oh, although you are devoid of form, you possess every form;
You know the object of all sense-organs, yet you have no sense-organs.

4.18.s:
sarasvatī jaḍībhūtā yatstotre yannirūpaṇe..
jaḍībhūto maheśaśca śeṣo dharmo vidhiḥ svayam.. 44 ..
4.18.d:
सरस्वती जडीभूता यत्स्तोत्रे यन्निरूपणे॥
जडीभूतो महेशश्च शेषो धर्मो विधिः स्वयम्॥ 44 ॥
4.18.m:
In praising whom and in defining whom Sarasvatī becomes stupefied,
And Maheśa, Śeṣa, Dharma, and Brahmā himself become stupefied,

4.18.s:
pārvatī kamalā rādhā sāvitrī vedasūrapi ..
vedaśca jaḍatāṃ yāti ke vā śaktā vipaścitaḥ .. 49 ..
4.18.d:
पार्वती कमला राधा सावित्री वेदसूरपि ॥
वेदश्च जडतां याति के वा शक्ता विपश्चितः ॥ 49 ॥
4.18.m:
As well as Pārvatī, Kamalā, Rādhā, and Sāvitrī, the mother of the Vedas,
And the Veda itself becomes struck dumb—what wise men then are capable?

4.18.s:
vayaṃ kiṃ stavanaṃ kurmaḥ striyaḥ prāṇeśvareśvara ..
prasanno bhava no deva dīnabandho kṛpāṃ kuru.. .. 46 ..
4.18.d:
वयं किं स्तवनं कुर्मः स्त्रियः प्राणेश्वरेश्वर ॥
प्रसन्नो भव नो देव दीनबन्धो कृपां कुरु॥ ॥ 46 ॥
4.18.m:
What praise can we women offer, O Lord of the Lord of our lives?
Be gracious to us, O God, O friend of the helpless, grant us mercy!

4.18.s:
iti petuśca tā viprapatnyastaccaraṇāmbuje ..
abhayaṃ pradadau tābhyaḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ ..47..
4.18.d:
इति पेतुश्च ता विप्रपत्न्यस्तच्चरणाम्बुजे ॥
अभयं प्रददौ ताभ्यः प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ॥47॥
4.18.m:
Having spoken thus, the brahmins' wives fell at his lotus feet.
With a pleased countenance and glance, he granted them freedom from fear.

4.18.s:
viprapatnīkṛtaṃ stotraṃ pūjākāle ca yaḥ paṭhet ..
sa gatiṃ viprapatnīnāṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 48 ..
4.18.d:
विप्रपत्नीकृतं स्तोत्रं पूजाकाले च यः पठेत् ॥
स गतिं विप्रपत्नीनां लभते नात्र संशयः ॥ 48 ॥
4.18.m:
Whoever recites this hymn composed by the brahmins' wives at the time of worship
Attains the destiny of the brahmins' wives; of this there is no doubt.

4.18.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca ..
tāḥ padāmbhojapatitā dṛṣṭvā śrīmadhusūdanaḥ ..
varaṃ vṛṇuta kalyāṇaṃ bhavitā cetyuvāca ha .. 49 ..
4.18.d:
नारायण उवाच ॥
ताः पदाम्भोजपतिता दृष्ट्वा श्रीमधुसूदनः ॥
वरं वृणुत कल्याणं भविता चेत्युवाच ह ॥ 49 ॥
4.18.m:
Seeing them fallen at his lotus feet, glorious Madhusūdana
Said: "Choose a boon; good fortune shall be yours!"

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā viprapantyo mudā'nvitāḥ..
tamūcurvacanaṃ bhaktyā bhaktinamrātmakandharāḥ ..4.18.50..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्णस्य वचः श्रुत्वा विप्रपन्त्यो मुदाऽन्विताः॥
तमूचुर्वचनं भक्त्या भक्तिनम्रात्मकन्धराः ॥4.18.50॥
4.18.m:
Hearing Śrī Kṛṣṇa's words, the brahmins' wives were filled with joy;
With their necks bowed in devotion, they addressed him in devotion:

4.18.s:
dvijapatnya ūcuḥ ..
varaṃ kṛṣṇa na gṛhṇīmo naḥ spṛhā tvatpadāmbuje ..
dehi svaṃ dāsyamasmabhyaṃ dṛḍhāṃ bhaktiṃ sudurlabhām .. 51 ..
4.18.d:
द्विजपत्न्य ऊचुः ॥
वरं कृष्ण न गृह्णीमो नः स्पृहा त्वत्पदाम्बुजे ॥
देहि स्वं दास्यमस्मभ्यं दृढां भक्तिं सुदुर्लभाम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.18.m:
"O Kṛṣṇa, we ask for no boon; our desire is for your lotus feet.
Grant us your service, and firm devotion, so very hard to attain!

4.18.s:
paśyāmo'nukṣaṇaṃ vaktrasarojaṃ tava keśava ..
anugrahaṃ kuru vibho na yāsyāmo gṛhaṃ punaḥ .. 52 ..
4.18.d:
पश्यामोऽनुक्षणं वक्त्रसरोजं तव केशव ॥
अनुग्रहं कुरु विभो न यास्यामो गृहं पुनः ॥ 52 ॥
4.18.m:
May we constantly behold your lotus face, O Keśava!
Show us favour, O Lord; we shall not return home again."

4.18.s:
dvijapatnīvacaḥ śrutvā śrīkṛṣṇaḥ karuṇānidhiḥ ..
omityuktvā trilokeśastasthau bālakasaṃsadi.. 53 ..
4.18.d:
द्विजपत्नीवचः श्रुत्वा श्रीकृष्णः करुणानिधिः ॥
ओमित्युक्त्वा त्रिलोकेशस्तस्थौ बालकसंसदि॥ 53 ॥
4.18.m:
Hearing the words of the brahmins' wives, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, an ocean of compassion,
Said "So be it," and the Lord of the three worlds remained in the assembly of boys.

4.18.s:
pradattaṃ viprapatnībhirmiṣṭamannaṃ sudhopamam ..
bālakānbhojayitvā tu svayaṃ ca bubhuje vibhuḥ..54..
4.18.d:
प्रदत्तं विप्रपत्नीभिर्मिष्टमन्नं सुधोपमम् ॥
बालकान्भोजयित्वा तु स्वयं च बुभुजे विभुः॥54॥
4.18.m:
Having fed the boys with the sweet food, nectar-like,
Offered by the brahmins' wives, the all-pervading Lord ate himself.

4.18.s:
etasminnantare tatra śātakumbhaṃ rathaṃ param ..
dadṛśurviprapatnyaśca patantaṃ gaganādaho ..55..
4.18.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र शातकुम्भं रथं परम् ॥
ददृशुर्विप्रपत्न्यश्च पतन्तं गगनादहो ॥55॥
4.18.m:
In the meantime, the brahmins' wives beheld an excellent golden chariot
Descending from the sky—oh, wonderful!

4.18.s:
ratnadarpaṇasaṃyuktaṃ ratnasāraparicchadam ..
ratnastambhairnibaddhaṃ ca sadratnakalaśojjvalam ..56..
4.18.d:
रत्नदर्पणसंयुक्तं रत्नसारपरिच्छदम् ॥
रत्नस्तम्भैर्निबद्धं च सद्रत्नकलशोज्ज्वलम् ॥56॥
4.18.m:
It was fitted with jewelled mirrors, covered with the finest gems,
Constructed with jewelled pillars, and radiant with pinnacles of fine jewels,

4.18.s:
śvetacāmarasaṃyuktaṃ vahniśuddhāṃśukānvitam ..
pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālājālairvirājitam..57..
4.18.d:
श्वेतचामरसंयुक्तं वह्निशुद्धांशुकान्वितम् ॥
पारिजातप्रसूनानां मालाजालैर्विराजितम्॥57॥
4.18.m: Furnished with white whisks, provided with fire-purified silk garments,

4.18.s:
śatacakrasamāyuktaṃ manoyāyi manoharam..
veṣṭitaṃ pārṣadairdivyairvanamālāvibhūṣitaiḥ...98 ..
4.18.d:
शतचक्रसमायुक्तं मनोयायि मनोहरम्॥
वेष्टितं पार्षदैर्दिव्यैर्वनमालाविभूषितैः॥.98 ॥
4.18.m:
Endowed with a hundred wheels, moving at the speed of thought, captivating,
Surrounded by divine attendants adorned with forest garlands,

4.18.s:
pītavastraparīdhānai ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitaiḥ ..
navayauvanasaṃpannaiḥ śyāmalaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ .. 59 ..
4.18.d:
पीतवस्त्रपरीधानै रत्नालंकारभूषितैः ॥
नवयौवनसंपन्नैः श्यामलैः सुमनोहरैः ॥ 59 ॥
4.18.m:
Wearing yellow garments, decorated with jewelled ornaments,
Possessed of fresh youth, dark-complexioned, exceedingly charming,

4.18.s:
dvibhujairmuralīhastairgopaveṣadharairvaraiḥ ..
śikhipicchaguñjamālābaddhavakrimacūḍakaiḥ .. 4.18.60 ..
4.18.d:
द्विभुजैर्मुरलीहस्तैर्गोपवेषधरैर्वरैः ॥
शिखिपिच्छगुञ्जमालाबद्धवक्रिमचूडकैः ॥ 4.18.60 ॥
4.18.m:
Two-armed, with flutes in hand, wearing the dress of cowherds, excellent,
With curved crests bound with peacock feathers and guñjā berry garlands.

4.18.s:
avaruhya rathāttūrṇaṃ te praṇamya hareḥ padam ..
rathamārohaṇaṃ kartumūcurbrāhmaṇakāminīḥ .. 61 ..
4.18.d:
अवरुह्य रथात्तूर्णं ते प्रणम्य हरेः पदम् ॥
रथमारोहणं कर्तुमूचुर्ब्राह्मणकामिनीः ॥ 61 ॥
4.18.m:
Quickly descending from the chariot and bowing to Hari's feet,
They told the brahmins' wives to mount the chariot.

4.18.s:
viprabhāryā hariṃ natvā jagmurgolokamīpsitam ..
babhūvurgopikāḥ sadyastyaktvā mānuṣavigrahān .. 62..
4.18.d:
विप्रभार्या हरिं नत्वा जग्मुर्गोलोकमीप्सितम् ॥
बभूवुर्गोपिकाः सद्यस्त्यक्त्वा मानुषविग्रहान् ॥ 62॥
4.18.m:
Bowing to Hari, the brahmins' wives went to desired Goloka;
Casting off their human bodies, they instantly became gopīs.

4.18.s:
hariśchāyāṃ vinirmāya tāsāṃ ca viṣṇumāyayā ..
prasthāpayāmāsa gṛhānbrāhmaṇānāṃ svayaṃ vibhuḥ .. 63 ..
4.18.d:
हरिश्छायां विनिर्माय तासां च विष्णुमायया ॥
प्रस्थापयामास गृहान्ब्राह्मणानां स्वयं विभुः ॥ 63 ॥
4.18.m:
Having created their shadow forms by Viṣṇu's illusory power,
Hari, the all-pervading Lord, himself sent them to the brahmins' homes.

4.18.s:
viprāśca bhāryā uddiśya paramodvignamānasāḥ ..
anveṣaṇaṃ prakurvanto dadṛśuḥ pathi kāminīḥ .. 64 ..
4.18.d:
विप्राश्च भार्या उद्दिश्य परमोद्विग्नमानसाः ॥
अन्वेषणं प्रकुर्वन्तो ददृशुः पथि कामिनीः ॥ 64 ॥
4.18.m:
The brahmins, their minds filled with extreme anxiety about their wives,
Searching for them, saw the women on the path.

4.18.s:
dṛṣṭvocurbrāhmaṇāḥ sarve tāste ca vinayānvitāḥ ..
pulakāṅkitasarvāṅgāḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇāḥ .. .. 65 ..
4.18.d:
दृष्ट्वोचुर्ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे तास्ते च विनयान्विताः ॥
पुलकाङ्कितसर्वाङ्गाः प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणाः ॥ ॥ 65 ॥
4.18.m:
Seeing them, all those brahmins, filled with humility,
Their limbs thrilling with horripilation, their faces and eyes cheerful, said:

4.18.s:
brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ ..
aho'tidhanyā yūyaṃ ca dṛṣṭo yuṣmābhirīśvaraḥ ..
asmākaṃ jīvanaṃ vyarthaṃ vedapāṭho'pyanarthakaḥ .. 66 ..
4.18.d:
ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः ॥
अहोऽतिधन्या यूयं च दृष्टो युष्माभिरीश्वरः ॥
अस्माकं जीवनं व्यर्थं वेदपाठोऽप्यनर्थकः ॥ 66 ॥
4.18.m:
"Oh, exceedingly fortunate are you, by whom the Lord has been seen!
Our life is useless, and our recitation of the Vedas is of no avail.

4.18.s:
vede purāṇe sarvatra vidvadbhiḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
harervibhūtayaḥ sarvāḥ sarveṣāṃ janako hariḥ .. 67 ..
4.18.d:
वेदे पुराणे सर्वत्र विद्वद्भिः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
हरेर्विभूतयः सर्वाः सर्वेषां जनको हरिः ॥ 67 ॥
4.18.m:
In the Veda, in the Purāṇas, and everywhere, the wise have proclaimed:
All things are manifestations of Hari; Hari is the father of all.

4.18.s:
tapo japo vrataṃ jñānaṃ vedā dhyayanamarcanam ..
tīrthasnānamanaśanaṃ sarveṣāṃ phalado hariḥ .. 68 ..
4.18.d:
तपो जपो व्रतं ज्ञानं वेदा ध्ययनमर्चनम् ॥
तीर्थस्नानमनशनं सर्वेषां फलदो हरिः ॥ 68 ॥
4.18.m:
Austerity, recitation, vows, knowledge, study of the Vedas, worship,
Bathing at holy places, and fasting—Hari is the giver of the fruit of them all!"

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇaḥ sevito yena kiṃ tasya tapasāṃ phalaiḥ ..
prāptaḥ kalpataruryena kiṃ tasyānyena śākhinā .. 69 ..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्णः सेवितो येन किं तस्य तपसां फलैः ॥
प्राप्तः कल्पतरुर्येन किं तस्यान्येन शाखिना ॥ 69 ॥
4.18.m:
For one by whom Śrī Kṛṣṇa is served, what need is there for the fruits of austerities?
For one who has attained the wish-fulfilling tree, what need is there for any other tree? // 69

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇo hṛdaye yasya tasya kiṃ karmabhiḥ kṛtaiḥ ..
kiṃ vā na sāgarasyaiva pauruṣaṃ kūpalaṅghane.. ..4.18.70..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्णो हृदये यस्य तस्य किं कर्मभिः कृतैः ॥
किं वा न सागरस्यैव पौरुषं कूपलङ्घने॥ ॥4.18.70॥
4.18.m:
For one in whose heart Śrī Kṛṣṇa resides, what need is there for performed rituals?
Or is there any prowess in jumping over a well for the ocean itself? // 70

4.18.s:
ityevamuktvā viprāśca gṛhītvā kāminīvarāḥ ..
ājagmuḥ svagṛhaṃ hṛṣṭāstābhiḥ sārdhaṃ ca remire ..71..
4.18.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा विप्राश्च गृहीत्वा कामिनीवराः ॥
आजग्मुः स्वगृहं हृष्टास्ताभिः सार्धं च रेमिरे ॥71॥
4.18.m:
Having spoken thus, the brahmins, taking their excellent wives,
went home delighted, and enjoyed pleasure with them. // 71

4.18.s:
tāsāṃ tato'dhikaṃ prema krīḍāsu sarvakarmasu ..
dākṣiṇyaṃ māyayā śaktyā brāhmaṇānāmatarkitam ..72..
4.18.d:
तासां ततोऽधिकं प्रेम क्रीडासु सर्वकर्मसु ॥
दाक्षिण्यं मायया शक्त्या ब्राह्मणानामतर्कितम् ॥72॥
4.18.m:
Greater than that was their love in sports and in all activities,
and their affection, unperceived by the brahmins, through his illusory power. // 72

4.18.s:
