atha nārāyaṇaḥ so'yaṃ balena śiśubhiḥ saha ..
jagāma svālayaṃ tūrṇaṃ pūrṇabrahma sanātanaḥ ..73..
4.18.d:
अथ नारायणः सोऽयं बलेन शिशुभिः सह ॥
जगाम स्वालयं तूर्णं पूर्णब्रह्म सनातनः ॥73॥
4.18.m:
Then that Nārāyaṇa, together with Balarāma and the children,
the eternal, complete Brahman, quickly went to his own abode. // 73

4.18.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ harermāhātmyamuttamam ..
purā śrutaṃ dharmavaktrātkiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. .. 74 ..
4.18.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं हरेर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥
पुरा श्रुतं धर्मवक्त्रात्किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ ॥ 74 ॥
4.18.m: as heard formerly from the mouth of Dharma. What more do you wish to hear? // 74

4.18.s:
nārada uvāca ..
ṛṣīndra kena puṇyena babhūva viprayoṣitām ..
munīndrayogasiddhānāṃ durlabhā gatirīśvarī .. 75 ..
4.18.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
ऋषीन्द्र केन पुण्येन बभूव विप्रयोषिताम् ॥
मुनीन्द्रयोगसिद्धानां दुर्लभा गतिरीश्वरी ॥ 75 ॥
4.18.m:
O best of ṛṣis, by what merit did the wives of the brahmins attain
that supreme state of the Lord, which is difficult even for the best of munis perfected in yoga to attain? // 75

4.18.s:
imāḥ kā vā puṇyavatyaḥ purā tasthurmahītalam ..
ājagmuḥ kena doṣeṇa vada saṃdehabhañjanam .. 76 ..
4.18.d:
इमाः का वा पुण्यवत्यः पुरा तस्थुर्महीतलम् ॥
आजग्मुः केन दोषेण वद संदेहभञ्जनम् ॥ 76 ॥
4.18.m:
Who were these virtuous women who previously dwelt on the surface of the earth?
By what fault did they arrive [there]? Speak, dispelling my doubt! // 76

4.18.s:
.. śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca..
saptarṣīṇāṃ ramaṇyaśca rūpeṇāpratimāḥ parāḥ ..
guṇavatyaḥ suśīlāśca dharmiṣṭhāśca pativratāḥ .. 77 ..
4.18.d:
॥ श्रीनारायण उवाच॥
सप्तर्षीणां रमण्यश्च रूपेणाप्रतिमाः पराः ॥
गुणवत्यः सुशीलाश्च धर्मिष्ठाश्च पतिव्रताः ॥ 77 ॥
4.18.m:
The wives of the Seven Ṛṣis were supreme, matchless in beauty,
virtuous, well-behaved, most righteous, and devoted wives. // 77

4.18.s:
navīnayauvanāḥ sarvāḥ pīnaśroṇi payodharāḥ ..
divyavastraparīdhānā ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ .. 78 ..
4.18.d:
नवीनयौवनाः सर्वाः पीनश्रोणि पयोधराः ॥
दिव्यवस्त्रपरीधाना रत्नालंकारभूषिताः ॥ 78 ॥
4.18.m: All were endowed with fresh youth, with plump hips and breasts,

4.18.s:
taptakāñcanavarṇābhāḥ smerānanasaroruhāḥ ..
munīnāṃ mohituṃ śaktā mānasaṃ vakracakṣuṣā .. 79 ..
4.18.d:
तप्तकाञ्चनवर्णाभाः स्मेराननसरोरुहाः ॥
मुनीनां मोहितुं शक्ता मानसं वक्रचक्षुषा ॥ 79 ॥
4.18.m:
having the lustrous hue of molten gold, with smiling lotus-like faces,
capable of enchanting the minds of munis with a sidelong glance. // 79

4.18.s:
dṛṣṭvā tāsāṃ stanaśroṇimukhāni sundarāṇi ca ..
analaścakame tāśca madanānalapīḍitaḥ .. 4.18.80 ..
4.18.d:
दृष्ट्वा तासां स्तनश्रोणिमुखानि सुन्दराणि च ॥
अनलश्चकमे ताश्च मदनानलपीडितः ॥ 4.18.80 ॥
4.18.m:
Seeing their breasts, hips, and beautiful faces,
Agni, afflicted by the fire of love, desired them. // 80

4.18.s:
agnisthānasthitānāṃ ca śikhayā suratonmukhaḥ ..
spṛṣṭvā cāṅgāni tāsāṃ ca babhūva hṛtacetanaḥ .. 81 ..
4.18.d:
अग्निस्थानस्थितानां च शिखया सुरतोन्मुखः ॥
स्पृष्ट्वा चाङ्गानि तासां च बभूव हृतचेतनः ॥ 81 ॥
4.18.m:
Longing for sexual union, through his flame [he approached] those who stood by the hearth,
and having touched their limbs, he lost his senses. // 81

4.18.s:
pativratā na jānanti patipādābjamānasāḥ ..
agniraṅgāni tāsāṃ ca darśaṃdarśaṃ mumoha ca .. 82 ..
4.18.d:
पतिव्रता न जानन्ति पतिपादाब्जमानसाः ॥
अग्निरङ्गानि तासां च दर्शंदर्शं मुमोह च ॥ 82 ॥
4.18.m:
The devoted wives did not notice, their minds fixed on the lotus-feet of their husbands;
and gazing repeatedly at their limbs, Agni was infatuated. // 82

4.18.s:
vahneśca mānasaṃ jñātvā bhagavānaṅgirā muniḥ ..
śaśāpa taṃ cetyuvāca sarvabhakṣo bhaveti ha .. 83 ..
4.18.d:
वह्नेश्च मानसं ज्ञात्वा भगवानङ्गिरा मुनिः ॥
शशाप तं चेत्युवाच सर्वभक्षो भवेति ह ॥ 83 ॥
4.18.m:
Perceiving the intention of the Fire, the venerable muni Aṅgiras
cursed him, saying: “Become an all-devourer!” // 83

4.18.s:
vahniḥ sacetano bhūtvā tuṣṭāva munipuṃgavam ..
vrīḍayā namravadanaścakampe brahmatejasā ..84 ..
4.18.d:
वह्निः सचेतनो भूत्वा तुष्टाव मुनिपुंगवम् ॥
व्रीडया नम्रवदनश्चकम्पे ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥84 ॥
4.18.m:
Regaining his senses, the Fire praised the eminent muni;
with face bowed down in shame, he trembled before his brahmanical splendour. // 84

4.18.s:
kruddho munivaraḥ spṛṣṭāḥ kāminyaśca śaśāpa ha ..
yāta yūyaṃ pāpayuktā mānuṣīṃ yonimeva ca .. 85 ..
4.18.d:
क्रुद्धो मुनिवरः स्पृष्टाः कामिन्यश्च शशाप ह ॥
यात यूयं पापयुक्ता मानुषीं योनिमेव च ॥ 85 ॥
4.18.m:
Enraged, the best of munis also cursed the lovely women who had been touched:
“Go, tainted with sin, to a human womb! // 85

4.18.s:
bhārate brāhmaṇānāṃ ca gṛhe labhata janma vai ..
kariṣyanti vivāhaṃ ca yuṣmākaṃ kulajā dvijāḥ .. 86 ..
4.18.d:
भारते ब्राह्मणानां च गृहे लभत जन्म वै ॥
करिष्यन्ति विवाहं च युष्माकं कुलजा द्विजाः ॥ 86 ॥
4.18.m:
Obtain birth indeed in the houses of brahmins in Bhārata!
Twice-born men born of noble families will marry you.” // 86

4.18.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ munestāśca ruruduḥ premavihvalāḥ ..
puṭāñjaliyutāḥ sarvā ūcustaṃ viduṣāṃ varam .. 87 ..
4.18.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं मुनेस्ताश्च रुरुदुः प्रेमविह्वलाः ॥
पुटाञ्जलियुताः सर्वा ऊचुस्तं विदुषां वरम् ॥ 87 ॥
4.18.m:
Hearing the words of the muni, they wept, agitated with love;
with folded hands, all of them said to that best of the learned: // 87

4.18.s:
munipatnya ūcuḥ ..
na tyajāsmānmuniśreṣṭha niṣpāpāśca pativratāḥ ..
ajānantyaḥ paraspṛṣṭā na ca nastyaktumarhasi .. 88..
4.18.d:
मुनिपत्न्य ऊचुः ॥
न त्यजास्मान्मुनिश्रेष्ठ निष्पापाश्च पतिव्रताः ॥
अजानन्त्यः परस्पृष्टा न च नस्त्यक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 88॥
4.18.m:
“Do not abandon us, O best of munis! We are sinless and devoted wives;
touched by another without our knowing, you ought not to abandon us! // 88

4.18.s:
bhaktānāṃ kiṃkarīṇāṃ ca na daṇḍaṃ kartumarhasi..
yuṣmākaṃ caraṇāmbhojaṃ kadā drakṣyāmahe vayam.. .. 89 ..
4.18.d:
भक्तानां किंकरीणां च न दण्डं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
युष्माकं चरणाम्भोजं कदा द्रक्ष्यामहे वयम्॥ ॥ 89 ॥
4.18.m:
You ought not to inflict punishment upon your devoted female servants.
When shall we behold your lotus-feet again? // 89

4.18.s:
khaḍgacchedādvajrapātātsarvapraharaṇānmune ..
dāruṇaḥ kāntavicchedaḥ sādhvīnāṃ duḥsahaḥ sadā .. 4.18.90 ..
4.18.d:
खड्गच्छेदाद्वज्रपातात्सर्वप्रहरणान्मुने ॥
दारुणः कान्तविच्छेदः साध्वीनां दुःसहः सदा ॥ 4.18.90 ॥
4.18.m:
Rather than the stroke of a sword, the fall of a thunderbolt, or any weapon, O muni,
separation from their beloved husband is cruel and always unbearable for virtuous women. // 90

4.18.s:
brahmiṣṭhānāṃ guṇavatāṃ parānkāntānmahāmunīn ..
evaṃbhūtānkathaṃ tyaktvā yāsyāmaḥ pṛthivītalam..91..
4.18.d:
ब्रह्मिष्ठानां गुणवतां परान्कान्तान्महामुनीन् ॥
एवंभूतान्कथं त्यक्त्वा यास्यामः पृथिवीतलम्॥91॥
4.18.m:
Devoted to Brahman, virtuous, supreme beloveds, great munis—
how can we abandon such husbands and go to the surface of the earth? // 91

4.18.s:
yāsyāmo yadi vipreśa kadā'trāgamanaṃ vada ..
ajñānasparśadoṣaśca na syānno vidhibodhitaḥ.. 92..
4.18.d:
यास्यामो यदि विप्रेश कदाऽत्रागमनं वद ॥
अज्ञानस्पर्शदोषश्च न स्यान्नो विधिबोधितः॥ 92॥
4.18.m:
If we must go, O lord of brahmins, tell us when our return here will be!
And may this fault of being touched unknowingly not be ordained for us by fate! // 92

4.18.s:
ahalyayā punaḥ prāptaḥ svāmīndrasya pradharṣaṇāt ..
sā saṃbhogātpunaḥ śuddhā sparśanādvarjitā vayam ..93..
4.18.d:
अहल्यया पुनः प्राप्तः स्वामीन्द्रस्य प्रधर्षणात् ॥
सा संभोगात्पुनः शुद्धा स्पर्शनाद्वर्जिता वयम् ॥93॥
4.18.m:
Her husband was regained by Ahalyā after being violated by Indra;
she was purified again after intercourse, while we are cast out merely from being touched! // 93

4.18.s:
vicāraṃ kuru dharmiṣṭha vedavedāṅgapāraga..
viśvakartuśca putrastvaṃ sarvavedavidāṃ vara..94 ..
4.18.d:
विचारं कुरु धर्मिष्ठ वेदवेदाङ्गपारग॥
विश्वकर्तुश्च पुत्रस्त्वं सर्ववेदविदां वर॥94 ॥
4.18.m:
Reflect on this, O most righteous one, master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas!
For you are the son of the creator of the universe, the foremost of all knowers of the Vedas. // 94

4.18.s:
anyeṣāṃ ca bhayātkāntā vrajanti śaraṇaṃ patim..
svakāntabhayasaṃvignāḥ śaraṇaṃ kaṃ vrajanti tāḥ ..95..
4.18.d:
अन्येषां च भयात्कान्ता व्रजन्ति शरणं पतिम्॥
स्वकान्तभयसंविग्नाः शरणं कं व्रजन्ति ताः ॥95॥
4.18.m:
Through fear of others, wives flee to their husband for refuge;
distressed by fear of their own husband, to whom shall they go for refuge? // 95

4.18.s:
abhayaṃ dehi dharmiṣṭha bhayayuktābhya eva ca..
putre śiṣye kalatre ca ko daṇḍaṃ kartumakṣamaḥ .. 96 ..
4.18.d:
अभयं देहि धर्मिष्ठ भययुक्ताभ्य एव च॥
पुत्रे शिष्ये कलत्रे च को दण्डं कर्तुमक्षमः ॥ 96 ॥
4.18.m:
Grant fearlessness, O most righteous one, to those who are filled with fear!
Over a son, a disciple, and a wife, who is incapable of inflicting punishment? // 96

4.18.s:
durbalaḥ sabalo vāpi svavastūnāmapīśvaraḥ ..
svadravyavikrayaṃ kartuṃ na cānyo rakṣituṃ kṣamaḥ ..97 ..
4.18.d:
दुर्बलः सबलो वापि स्ववस्तूनामपीश्वरः ॥
स्वद्रव्यविक्रयं कर्तुं न चान्यो रक्षितुं क्षमः ॥97 ॥
4.18.m:
Whether weak or strong, one is the master of one's own possessions.
[Only he is able] to sell his own property, and no other can preserve it. // 97

4.18.s:
kāminīnāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā dayālurmunipuṃgavaḥ ..
premṇā ruroda tāsāṃ ca nirīkṣya mukhapaṅkajam ..98..
4.18.d:
कामिनीनां वचः श्रुत्वा दयालुर्मुनिपुंगवः ॥
प्रेम्णा रुरोद तासां च निरीक्ष्य मुखपङ्कजम् ॥98॥
4.18.m:
Hearing the words of the women, the compassionate foremost among sages,
gazing upon their lotus-like faces, wept out of love. // 98

4.18.s:
vedavedāṅgapārajño jñānināṃ yogināṃ varaḥ ..
patnīvicchedaviṣaye mūrcchāṃ prāpa tathāpi saḥ ..99..
4.18.d:
वेदवेदाङ्गपारज्ञो ज्ञानिनां योगिनां वरः ॥
पत्नीविच्छेदविषये मूर्च्छां प्राप तथापि सः ॥99॥
4.18.m:
Though he had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, the best among knowers and yogins,
he nevertheless fainted at the prospect of separation from his wife. // 99

4.18.s:
sarve babhūvuḥ śokārtā virahodvignamānasāḥ..
nirīkṣya tāsāṃ vaktrāṇi tasthuḥ puttalikā yathā.. .. 4.18.100 ..
4.18.d:
सर्वे बभूवुः शोकार्ता विरहोद्विग्नमानसाः॥
निरीक्ष्य तासां वक्त्राणि तस्थुः पुत्तलिका यथा॥ ॥ 4.18.100 ॥
4.18.m:
All of them became stricken with grief, their minds agitated by separation;
gazing at their faces, they stood like statues. // 4.18.100

4.18.s:
kṛtvā vilāpaṃ suciraṃ sarvavedavidāṃ varaḥ ..
bhrātṛbhiśca sahālocya tā uvāca śucā''turaḥ ..101..
4.18.d:
कृत्वा विलापं सुचिरं सर्ववेदविदां वरः ॥
भ्रातृभिश्च सहालोच्य ता उवाच शुचा'ऽतुरः ॥101॥
4.18.m:
Having lamented for a very long time, the best of all knowers of the Vedas,
deliberating together with his brothers, spoke to them, afflicted with sorrow: // 101

4.18.s:
aṅgirā uvāca ..
yūyaṃ śṛṇuta vakṣyāmi vacanaṃ satyameva ca ..
svakarmabhogināṃ bhogamākarmācca śrutau śrutam .. 102 ..
4.18.d:
अङ्गिरा उवाच ॥
यूयं शृणुत वक्ष्यामि वचनं सत्यमेव च ॥
स्वकर्मभोगिनां भोगमाकर्माच्च श्रुतौ श्रुतम् ॥ 102 ॥
4.18.m:
"Listen, I shall speak words that are truly true.
In the Veda it is heard that the experience of those who enjoy their own karma lasts until the karma is exhausted. // 102

4.18.s:
gato bhogaśca yuṣmākamasmābhiḥ saha niścitam ..
gate bhoge punarbhogo na hi vede nirūpitaḥ .. 103 ..
4.18.d:
गतो भोगश्च युष्माकमस्माभिः सह निश्चितम् ॥
गते भोगे पुनर्भोगो न हि वेदे निरूपितः ॥ 103 ॥
4.18.m:
Your experience with us is certainly ended.
When experience has ended, repeated experience is nowhere established in the Veda. // 103

4.18.s:
śubhāśubhaṃ ca yatkarma bhārate kṛtibhiḥ saha ..
nābhuktaṃ kṣīyate karma janmakoṭiśatairapi .. 104 ..
4.18.d:
शुभाशुभं च यत्कर्म भारते कृतिभिः सह ॥
नाभुक्तं क्षीयते कर्म जन्मकोटिशतैरपि ॥ 104 ॥
4.18.m:
Whatever karma, auspicious or inauspicious, is performed in Bhārata by agents,
karma is not exhausted without being experienced, even in hundreds of millions of births. // 104

4.18.s:
parabhuktāṃ ca kāntāṃ ca yo bhuṅkte sa narādhamaḥ ..
sa pacyate kālasūtre yāvaccandradivākarau .. 109 ..
4.18.d:
परभुक्तां च कान्तां च यो भुङ्क्ते स नराधमः ॥
स पच्यते कालसूत्रे यावच्चन्द्रदिवाकरौ ॥ 109 ॥
4.18.m:
He who enjoys a beloved woman who has been enjoyed by another is the lowest of men;
he is cooked in Kālasūtra as long as the moon and the sun endure. // 109

4.18.s:
na sā daive na sā paitrye pākārhā pāpasaṃyutā ..
tasyā āliṃgane bhartā bhraṣṭaśrīstejasā hataḥ .. 106 ..
4.18.d:
न सा दैवे न सा पैत्र्ये पाकार्हा पापसंयुता ॥
तस्या आलिंगने भर्ता भ्रष्टश्रीस्तेजसा हतः ॥ 106 ॥
4.18.m:
She is not fit for cooking in rites for gods or ancestors, being tainted with sin.
By embracing her, a husband loses his fortune and is struck down in his splendour. // 106

4.18.s:
devatāḥ pitarastasya havyadāne ca tarpaṇe ..
sukhino na bhavantyevamityāha kamalodbhavaḥ .. 107 ..
4.18.d:
देवताः पितरस्तस्य हव्यदाने च तर्पणे ॥
सुखिनो न भवन्त्येवमित्याह कमलोद्भवः ॥ 107 ॥
4.18.m:
Neither the deities nor his ancestors are pleased with his offerings of oblations
and libations of water; thus said the Lotus-born [Brahmā]. // 107

4.18.s:
tasmādyatnena bhāryāyā rakṣaṇaṃ kurute sudhīḥ ..
anyathā pāpabhāgbhartā niścitaṃ narakaṃ vrajet .. 108..
4.18.d:
तस्माद्यत्नेन भार्याया रक्षणं कुरुते सुधीः ॥
अन्यथा पापभाग्भर्ता निश्चितं नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ 108॥
4.18.m:
Therefore, an intelligent man carefully protects his wife;
otherwise, sharing in sin, the husband will certainly go to hell. // 108

4.18.s:
padepade sāvadhānaḥ kāntāṃ rakṣati paṇḍitaḥ ..
na vratī na sthalī yoṣā doṣāṇāṃ ca karaṇḍikā .. 109 ..
4.18.d:
पदेपदे सावधानः कान्तां रक्षति पण्डितः ॥
न व्रती न स्थली योषा दोषाणां च करण्डिका ॥ 109 ॥
4.18.m:
At every step, a wise man protects his wife with vigilance;
a woman is not bound by vows nor fixed in place; she is a basket of faults. // 109

4.18.s:
kalatraṃ pākapātraṃ ca sadā rakṣitumarhati ..
parasparśādaśuddhāṃ ca śuddhāṃ svasparśane sadā .. 4.18.110 ..
4.18.d:
कलत्रं पाकपात्रं च सदा रक्षितुमर्हति ॥
परस्पर्शादशुद्धां च शुद्धां स्वस्पर्शने सदा ॥ 4.18.110 ॥
4.18.m:
One should always guard one's wife and one's cooking vessel:
she is defiled by the touch of another, but always pure in one's own touch. // 4.18.110

4.18.s:
svakāntaṃ ca parityajya paraṃ gacchati yā'dhamā ..
kumbhīpākaṃ sā prayāti yāvaccandradivākarau .. 111 ..
4.18.d:
स्वकान्तं च परित्यज्य परं गच्छति याऽधमा ॥
कुम्भीपाकं सा प्रयाति यावच्चन्द्रदिवाकरौ ॥ 111 ॥
4.18.m:
That base woman who abandons her own husband and goes to another
goes to Kumbhīpāka as long as the moon and the sun endure. // 111

4.18.s:
tāmeva yamadūtāśca saṃsthāpya narakāntare ..
uttiṣṭhati vidūrāccetkurvanti daṇḍatāḍanām .. 112 ..
4.18.d:
तामेव यमदूताश्च संस्थाप्य नरकान्तरे ॥
उत्तिष्ठति विदूराच्चेत्कुर्वन्ति दण्डताडनाम् ॥ 112 ॥
4.18.m:
Placing that very woman within the hell, the messengers of Yama
strike her with rods if she stands up from a distance. // 112

4.18.s:
sarpapramāṇāḥ kīṭāśca tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāḥ sudāruṇāḥ ..
daśanti puṃścalīṃ tatra satataṃ ca divāniśam .. 113 ..
4.18.d:
सर्पप्रमाणाः कीटाश्च तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राः सुदारुणाः ॥
दशन्ति पुंश्चलीं तत्र सततं च दिवानिशम् ॥ 113 ॥
4.18.m:
Worms as large as serpents, with sharp fangs and terrifying,
bite that unchaste woman there continuously, day and night. // 113

4.18.s:
vikṛtākāraśabdaṃ ca karoti śāśvataṃ bhiyā ..
na mamāra prahāreṇa sūkṣmadehavidhāriṇī .. 114 ..
4.18.d:
विकृताकारशब्दं च करोति शाश्वतं भिया ॥
न ममार प्रहारेण सूक्ष्मदेहविधारिणी ॥ 114 ॥
4.18.m:
She constantly makes hideous sounds out of fear;
possessing a subtle body, she does not die from the beating. // 114

4.18.s:
muhūrtārdhaṃ sukhaṃ bhuktvā loke'tra yaśasā hatā ..
patitā paraloke ca gatimetādṛśīṃ labhet .. 115 ..
4.18.d:
मुहूर्तार्धं सुखं भुक्त्वा लोकेऽत्र यशसा हता ॥
पतिता परलोके च गतिमेतादृशीं लभेत् ॥ 115 ॥
4.18.m:
Having enjoyed pleasure for half a muhūrta, ruined in reputation in this world,
fallen, in the next world she obtains such a destination. // 115

4.18.s:
paraspṛṣṭā ca vai nārī yā spṛhāṃ kurute param ..
sā'pi duṣṭā parityājyā cetyāha kamalodbhavaḥ .. 116 ..
4.18.d:
परस्पृष्टा च वै नारी या स्पृहां कुरुते परम् ॥
साऽपि दुष्टा परित्याज्या चेत्याह कमलोद्भवः ॥ 116 ॥
4.18.m:
Even a woman touched by another who then yearns for someone else,
she too, being wicked, is to be abandoned; so said the Lotus-born [Brahmā]. // 116

4.18.s:
tasmānnārī parairyatnādadṛṣṭā kṛtibhiḥ kṛtā ..
asūryaṃpaśyā yā dārāḥ śuddhāstāśca pativratāḥ .. 117 ..
4.18.d:
तस्मान्नारी परैर्यत्नाददृष्टा कृतिभिः कृता ॥
असूर्यंपश्या या दाराः शुद्धास्ताश्च पतिव्रताः ॥ 117 ॥
4.18.m:
Therefore, a woman is carefully kept unseen by others by wise men;
wives who are not seen even by the sun are pure, devoted wives. // 117

4.18.s:
svacchandagāminī yā ca svatantrā sūkarīsamā ..
antarduṣṭā sadā saiva niścitaṃ paragāminī .. 118 ..
4.18.d:
स्वच्छन्दगामिनी या च स्वतन्त्रा सूकरीसमा ॥
अन्तर्दुष्टा सदा सैव निश्चितं परगामिनी ॥ 118 ॥
4.18.m:
She who moves about at will and is independent like a sow,
is always corrupt within and certainly goes after other men. // 118

4.18.s:
svāmisādhyā ca yā nārī kuladharmabhiyā sthitā ..
kāntena sārddhaṃ sā kāntā vaikuṇṭhaṃ yāti niścitam .. 119 ..
4.18.d:
स्वामिसाध्या च या नारी कुलधर्मभिया स्थिता ॥
कान्तेन सार्द्धं सा कान्ता वैकुण्ठं याति निश्चितम् ॥ 119 ॥
4.18.m:
A woman who is devoted to her husband and remains steadfast out of fear of family duty,
that beloved wife certainly goes to Vaikuṇṭha together with her husband. // 119

4.18.s:
yāta yūyaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ mānuṣīṃ yonimīpsitām ..
kṛṣṇadarśanamātreṇa golokaṃ yāsyatha dhruvam ..4.18.120..
4.18.d:
यात यूयं च पृथिवीं मानुषीं योनिमीप्सिताम् ॥
कृष्णदर्शनमात्रेण गोलोकं यास्यथ ध्रुवम् ॥4.18.120॥
4.18.m:
Go, then, to the earth into the desired human womb;
by merely beholding Kṛṣṇa, you will surely go to Goloka. // 4.18.120

4.18.s:
hariṇā nirmitāśchāyā yuṣmākaṃ yogamāyayā ..
tā vipramandire sthitvā cāgamiṣyanti no dhruvam ..121..
4.18.d:
हरिणा निर्मिताश्छाया युष्माकं योगमायया ॥
ता विप्रमन्दिरे स्थित्वा चागमिष्यन्ति नो ध्रुवम् ॥121॥
4.18.m:
Shadows of you have been fashioned by Hari through Yogamāyā;
remaining in the brāhmaṇa's house, they will surely not return to us. // 121

4.18.s:
punaraṃśena naḥ patnyo bhaviṣyatha na saṃśayaḥ ..
yuṣmākaṃ mama śāpaśca babhūva ca varādhikaḥ .. 122 ..
4.18.d:
पुनरंशेन नः पत्न्यो भविष्यथ न संशयः ॥
युष्माकं मम शापश्च बभूव च वराधिकः ॥ 122 ॥
4.18.m:
You shall again become our wives by a portion, there is no doubt;
and my curse upon you has become greater than a boon." // 122

4.18.s:
ityevamuktvā sa munirvirarāma śucā'nvitaḥ ..
tā āgatya mahīṃ śāpādbabhūvurviprayoṣitaḥ .. 123 ..
4.18.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स मुनिर्विरराम शुचाऽन्वितः ॥
ता आगत्य महीं शापाद्बभूवुर्विप्रयोषितः ॥ 123 ॥
4.18.m:
Having spoken thus, the sage fell silent, filled with grief.
They, having come to earth due to the curse, became the wives of brāhmaṇas. // 123

4.18.s:
dattvā'nnaṃ haraye bhaktyā prajagmurharimandiram ..
babhūva niścitaṃ tāsāṃ śāpaśca saṃpado'dhikaḥ .. 124 ..
4.18.d:
दत्त्वाऽन्नं हरये भक्त्या प्रजग्मुर्हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
बभूव निश्चितं तासां शापश्च संपदोऽधिकः ॥ 124 ॥
4.18.m:
Having given food to Hari with devotion, they went to the abode of Hari;
for them, the curse certainly became greater than prosperity. // 124

4.18.s:
nindyā nīcā ca saṃpattirvipattirmahato varā ..
aho sadyaḥ satāṃ kopaścopakārāya kalpate .. 125 ..
4.18.d:
निन्द्या नीचा च संपत्तिर्विपत्तिर्महतो वरा ॥
अहो सद्यः सतां कोपश्चोपकाराय कल्पते ॥ 125 ॥
4.18.m:
Lowly fortune is reprehensible, whereas misfortune from the great is superior;
ah, the anger of the virtuous immediately serves to bring about benefit! // 125

4.18.s:
vinā vipattermahimā kutaḥ kasya bhavedbhuvi ..
bhūtāḥ kāntaparityāgānmuktā brāhmaṇayoṣitaḥ .. 126 ..
4.18.d:
विना विपत्तेर्महिमा कुतः कस्य भवेद्भुवि ॥
भूताः कान्तपरित्यागान्मुक्ता ब्राह्मणयोषितः ॥ 126 ॥
4.18.m:
Without misfortune, whence would greatness come to anyone on earth?
By being abandoned by their husbands, the brāhmaṇa women attained liberation. // 126

4.18.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ hareścaritamuttamam ..
aho puṇyavatīnāṃ ca mokṣākhyānaṃ manoharam .. 127 ..
4.18.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं हरेश्चरितमुत्तमम् ॥
अहो पुण्यवतीनां च मोक्षाख्यानं मनोहरम् ॥ 127 ॥
4.18.m:
Thus all the supreme deeds of Hari have been narrated,
as well as the delightful account of the liberation of those virtuous women.

4.18.s:
śrīkṛṣṇākhyānaṃ viprendra nūtnaṃ nūtnaṃ padepade ..
na hi tṛptiḥ śrutavatāṃ kena śreyasi tṛpyate .. 128 ..
4.18.d:
श्रीकृष्णाख्यानं विप्रेन्द्र नूत्नं नूत्नं पदेपदे ॥
न हि तृप्तिः श्रुतवतां केन श्रेयसि तृप्यते ॥ 128 ॥
4.18.m:
The account of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, O best of brahmins, is ever new at every step;
for those who hear it, there is never satiety: who is ever satiated with the highest good?

4.18.s:
yāvadramyaṃ tatkathitaṃ yacchrutaṃ guruvaktrataḥ ..
vada māṃ vāñchitaṃ yatte kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 129 ..
4.18.d:
यावद्रम्यं तत्कथितं यच्छ्रुतं गुरुवक्त्रतः ॥
वद मां वाञ्छितं यत्ते किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 129 ॥
4.18.m:
As far as it is delightful, that which was heard from the mouth of the guru has been told.
Tell me what you desire: what more do you wish to hear?

4.18.s:
nārada uvāca ..
yadyacchrutaṃ tvayā pūrvaṃ guruvaktrātkṛpānidhe ..
maṅgalaṃ kṛṣṇacaritaṃ tanme brūhi jagadguro .. 4.18.130 ..
4.18.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
यद्यच्छ्रुतं त्वया पूर्वं गुरुवक्त्रात्कृपानिधे ॥
मङ्गलं कृष्णचरितं तन्मे ब्रूहि जगद्गुरो ॥ 4.18.130 ॥
4.18.m:
Whatever was heard by you formerly from the mouth of your guru, O ocean of compassion,
that auspicious life of Kṛṣṇa, tell me that, O guru of the universe!

4.18.s:
sūta uvāca ..
śrutvā devarṣivacanamṛṣirnārāyaṇaḥ svayam ..
aparaṃ kṛṣṇamāhātmyaṃ pravaktumupacakrame.. 131 ..
iti śrībrahmavaivarte mahāpurāṇre śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍe viprapatnīmokṣa ṇaprastāvonāmāṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 18 ..
4.18.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
श्रुत्वा देवर्षिवचनमृषिर्नारायणः स्वयम् ॥
अपरं कृष्णमाहात्म्यं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे॥ 131 ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्मवैवर्ते महापुराण्रे श्रीकृष्णजन्मखण्डे विप्रपत्नीमोक्ष णप्रस्तावोनामाष्टादशोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
4.18.m:
Hearing the words of the divine sage, the sage Nārāyaṇa himself
undertook to narrate further the greatness of Kṛṣṇa.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, entitled 'The Episode of the Liberation of the Brahmin Wives,' in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa of the great Purāṇa, the glorious Brahmavaivarta.
